News.title: Fury as spooky ‘effigies’ suddenly appear at roadside in bizarre long-running neighbour row – with kids left terrified
News.content:
SCARE TACTIC Fury as spooky ‘effigies’ suddenly appear at roadside in bizarre long-running neighbour row – with kids left terrified

VILLAGERS have been left furious as spooky “effigies” suddenly appeared on a quiet country lane, leaving children terrified.

Creepy dummies and stuffed figurines have been carefully arranged on the roadside of Court Hill in Littlebourne, near Canterbury following a long-running neighbour row.



Villagers have been baffled by who is responsible for the bizarre display, prompting complaints about it scaring kids and distracting motorists.

Along with stuffed old fancy-dress costumes, skeletons, and homemade signs, there are several more hanging from a metal gate near a caravan.



Some of the characters are standing up, while others sit down on the grass, wearing unsettling masks with creepy smiles.

One enormous orange creature holds a handwritten sign reading “Dumped here” and “Aspbestos”.

There is also an old-fashioned pram that has a dummy dressed in black and a top hat, hanging on to one side.

The creepy homemade dummies appeared as part of a dispute between a woman living in a caravan and an agricultural business.



Stevie Lowe moved on to land owned by EH Holdstock & Son two years ago – but the business says she did so without permission.

Despite being issued with “official notices”, Stevie has refused to leave the site and has started filling the area with the strange effigies.

Stevie says the display is intended to draw attention to a long-running disagreement over material found near the site which she claims contains asbestos.

It’s not been established what the material is or who originally left it there.

Stevie said: “I informed the farmer and asked him to move it.”



Despite the attention they have attracted, Stevie says the collection is far from finished.

“I’ve got four more effigies to put up,” she said.

Her partner, Dereck Owens, said: “We found the asbestos two years ago in August, so it could have been here for any amount of time before that.”

Stevie says she has refused to leave while it remains there, arguing she is concerned for relatives and other families living nearby.

“Move it, and then I’ll move,” she said. “That’s it. Simple.”



But EH Holdstock & Son strongly disputes her account, saying: “They have never been given permission to be there.

“The correct procedures have been followed and they have been issued numerous official notices to leave in the presence of the police.

“The farm is working with the police, city council, parish council and the courts in addressing the matter.”

The company also alleges the pair have moved asbestos around the land, restricted access, verbally abused staff and vandalised farm equipment.

Stevie admitted she did not ask for permission to move onto the land, but claimed she had previously been told she could stay and strongly denies vandalising equipment or abusing staff.



However, she confirmed she had moved the material she believes is asbestos to the farm’s gates.

Stevie says she was issued with two notices to leave, but claims they did not appear to be from a solicitor.

Meanwhile, the effigies have continued to multiply, with Stevie saying she is aware of complaints about the display and claims she has been told some children find the figures scary.

But she has no plans to take them down while the dispute continues.

Canterbury City Council says there is no active planning enforcement case at the site and that, as it is privately owned, the authority has no involvement in the dispute or rubbish there.

Kent Police also searched its records and said it could find no relevant incidents at Court Hill from the beginning of this year.

A spokesperson said the circumstances appeared to be “more of a civil matter than a policing one currently”.

News.title: Eight rapes in just 20 days on Brit holiday island as hospital is ‘at breaking point’ with tourist-related injuries
News.content:
ISLAND RAPE HELL Eight rapes in just 20 days on Brit holiday island as hospital is ‘at breaking point’ with tourist-related injuries

FEARS are rising for women on an island in Greece after eight rapes were reported in 20 days.

Allegations of sexual abuse have rocked Zante, popular among tourists – particularly Brits – for its vibrant nightlife and stunning beaches.



Michalis Giannakos, president of public healthcare workers’ union POEDIN, said that eight female tourists sought medical attention, reporting that they had been raped.

He said: “It is abhorrent and humiliating what is happening to the women, with individuals taking advantage of the state of intoxication in which they may be.”



Most of the attacks are reportedly linked to the popular area of Laganas.

Police were deployed, and forensic examinations were carried out by the hospital’s gynaecologists.

If you have been affected by the issues raised in the article, please reach out to jeylin.mehmet@news.co.uk

No prosecutions were brought forward as the women reportedly refused to name the alleged perpetrators and did not file charges, as reported by local media.

Giannakos added that a few days ago an Italian tourist needed specialised medical treatment to treat injuries that, according to her, were caused after rape.

A statement from police said: “During the period from May to August 6, three incidents have been reported to our competent service, for which all procedures provided for by law were immediately followed, in cooperation with the prosecutor’s office, forensic and health authorities, and two arrests have been made.”



This comes as two 18-year-old British women have accused a man in Zante of raping them.

Both victims told police they were raped by the same man, according to local media outlet Ethnos.

An urgent probe after the pair were taken to hospital to undergo medical examination.

Upon hearing the horror allegations, the mother of one of the women immediately drove from the UK to Greece.

She managed to track down the suspect to his place of work and attacked him, according to local media.



Officers were called to the scene and the mother and suspect were both taken to the police station.

The suspect has since been arrested on suspicion of rape with a case filed against him.

Authorities are now investigating the complaints and the circumstances around the alleged incidents.

In a separate case, two British sisters were allegedly raped by two UK tourist brothers in Rhodes.

Greece has seen sexual violence cases increase sharply over the past 14 years, with police recording 1,250 offences in 2024 compared to just 511 in 2010, according to the latest Eurostat data.



That marks a 145 per cent rise, one of the steeper climbs recorded across the European Union during the same period.

News.title: Three dead after helicopter crashes shortly following take-off on Greece holiday island as emergency crews rush to scene
News.content:
AT least three people have been killed in a horror helicopter crash in Greece – as emergency services rush to the scene.

The chopper went down on the holiday hotspot island of Sifnos shortly after taking off – leaving the pilot and two passengers dead.



The small private helicopter is said to have exploded and gone up in a huge fireball upon impact this evening.

A huge inferno broke out before two firefighters and one fire engine raced to the site to tackle the raging flames, according to local media.



A rescue team from Syros then arrived later on with the Fire Department’s RAFNAR speedboat.

It is currently unclear what caused the helicopter to crash.

It is understood that the pilot was Greek while the two passengers were foreigners.

Images shown in local reports showed what appeared to be the crash site on an arid hillside.



Plumes of smoke could be seen billowing from a raging fire near shrubs and bushes.

The chopper, reportedly a Bell 206 helicopter, had just taken off from the island’s helipad in the Tholos area.

The aircraft plunged towards the ground just seconds after taking off, according to the Kathimerini Daily.

It came down and went up in a vicious fireball in an inhabited area – but no homes were hit, it is understood.

The pilot was reportedly hired just two months ago, according to local reports.



One witness told local outlet SKAI that the helicopter began to spin around at a high speed before it smashed into the ground.

Manolis Fountoulakis, deputy mayor of Sifnos, told Greek channel Alpha: “It experienced mechanical failure in the air, residents say it made a loud, strange noise, like military aircraft.”

The Greek fire service said the crash triggered an alarm heard across the island – a popular tourist destination over the summer season.

News.title: Teens’ college places will be fully funded to help youth inactivity crisis, Ministers say
News.content:
ALL college places will be fully-funded for 16-19 year-olds to help reduce youth inactivity numbers.

Education Secretary Lucy Powell says the cash will be guaranteed for all courses following GCSE results on Thursday.



Teenagers can show up knowing that colleges will be able to afford it in an effort to reduce the one million 16-24 year-olds not earning or learning.

Previously, colleges wouldn’t know if they would get extra funding if more students turned up.



Cabinet Minister Ms Powell said: “Results day was proof of the vital work colleges are doing, delivering lifechanging learning to hundreds of thousands of young people across the country.

“With record numbers receiving T Level results this year, it’s clear demand for high-quality technical education is growing fast.

“But for too long, colleges have only heard warm words from government. I am determined to back them with actions.

“This guarantee means colleges can offer places to every young person who wants one, driving down the number of young people not in education or training, and giving them the skills, experience and confidence to thrive.”

It follows Andy Burnham saying secondary school pupils from aged 14 will be able to study subjects such as AI and manufacturing under major reforms.

He said he was on a “mission” to reduce the number of Neets – those not in education, employment or training – which currently sits at more than one million youngsters.



Labour grandee Alan Milburn is currently conducting a review into the crisis and will publish his report in the autumn.

The PM last month said: “We’ve had a system built for too long around the university route and it sends a message to some young people that they’re some kind of second-class citizens, and it’s just not right.

“They need an education system that works for them as well, that offers a path to all young people, that’s balanced between academic and technical.”

News.title: First look at UK’s ‘golf course by the sea’ as multi-million pound plans are EXPANDED
News.content:
A FIRST look has been given to the UK’s ‘golf course by the sea’ as multi-million pound plans for the development are expanded.

The mega-scheme, which has not finished completion yet, is set to cost £120million in total.



GSE Group, which operates Kent-based Hythe Golf Club and Hythe Imperial Hotel, has now revealed even bigger plans for its Imperial Gardens proposal.

The beachfront scheme is set to transform the hotel’s current 40-acre site into a mixed-use destination, with housing, leisure facilities and new golf course added to the area.



Around 291 homes are also set to built on the part of the land, with 25 per cent affordable.

A newly expanded 25metre swimming pool and purpose-built gym will also be constructed, which will be available for residents, community members (including schools and youth groups), as well as hotel guests to use.

Under new plans, the buffer zone alongside the Royal Military Canal has also been widened, following concerns from the community regarding the protection of the waterway.

The £120million project also intends to improve the Hythe Imperial Hotel’s current offering.



This includes replacing the existing 18-hole golf course with a new nine-hole three-par course, as well as a themed adventure golf area.

GSE Group chairman, Darrell Healey, told Kent Online: “We have listened to the community, and our proposals now offer even ‘more for Hythe’.

“Our plans have evolved from the previous tourism-led scheme to now focusing on the combination of a new extended leisure offering across multiple sports and activities.”



Initially opened in 1880, Hythe Imperial Hotel was bought by GSE Group in 2007.

Plans for the project were initially announced in November last year, and have undergone a number of revisions since.

News.title: Mum of boy, 5, who fell to death from 15th floor window blasts ‘he’d still be here if council had listened to me’
News.content:
PLUNGE TRAGEDY Mum of boy, 5, who fell to death from 15th floor window blasts ‘he’d still be here if council had listened to me’

THE mum of a five-year-old boy who fell to his death from a 15th-floor window told an inquest he still “could have been here” if the council had done its job properly.

Aalim Ahmed was killed instantly when he landed on railings at the bottom of a block of flats in Plaistow, East London.



The youngster’s body was discovered by his dad shortly before 6am on May 16, 2024.

Aalim’s mum Sahra Osman told Walthamstow Coroner’s Court she was “scared” and “horrified” when Newham Council put them in the top-floor flat, which needed repairs.



She expressed concerns about the top-floor flat in Jacobs House in February 2023 and felt it was not suitable for Aalim and his toddler sibling.

But the mum claimed she was told to move in first and then complain or risk being made homeless if she turned the property down.



Sahra said the windows had “faulty” restrictors and her ongoing complaints to get them fixed led only to a series of workmen who did not sort the problem.

The mum told the court that when a window engineer came in January 2024, she tried “all the windows” in the flat and she could still open them.

She wanted a safety device, called a restrictor, on all the windows and noted the bedroom window could be left “just open wide”, saying “I was quite scared and it was unsafe”.

The engineer said he would see about getting it fixed but within a day she found a window restrictor on the floor.



She called the council to complain and begged them to help, telling the inquest “the window was wide open, it would not lock, it was hanging”, and she wanted to speak to a manager.

Sahra stressed it was a safety issue for her children, but said the council did not treat it as “an emergency”.

The mum said the “restrictors were not working, they were there for decoration” and she was frustrated as it could take months to get a proper response from the council.

But the council suggested the engineer was not told of any issues with the restrictor in the kitchen but there were problems in the living room.

Sahra claimed she insisted she told the workmen there was a problem in all the rooms and accused the council of “not taking my situation seriously enough”.



She also told the council her son had autism and “no sense of danger” in an email and “believes” she also sent a letter about his diagnosis.

The mum added: “You guys could have prevented this tragic thing from happening. If you had done your job, he could have been here.

“I think that Newham Council failed me as a mum, as a tenant.

“I tried everything. I tried to tell them my concerns about safety multiple time and you guys ignored me rather than doing anything about the actual issues.

“I told you my son (Aalim) has autism.



“I do not know what more I can prove. I showed you a GP letter. The people that knew him sent a letter to the council saying this family need to be moved from this flat because they are not safe.”

Reliving the horror, Sahra said she believes her son may have been reaching for a biscuit when he fell from the window.

She told the inquest the windows were “always closed” before the family went to bed.

The court heard Sahra’s screams alerted Aalim’s dad Makail Ahmed, who was “screaming in shock” when he saw the youngster’s pyjamas.

Makail told the inquest the moment he found his son was one of “disbelief – it was a nightmare.”



The inquest continues.

News.title: My mum died after being stabbed in eye by ex freed from jail two weeks earlier…danger signs were missed in broken system
News.content:
WHEN her abusive ex was released from jail, caring Michaela Hall was manipulated into taking him back into her home. Just two weeks later, Lee Kendall stabbed her to death in a row over a meal she had cooked him.

Now her teenage son, Shaun Hall – who was just 13 when his mum was brutally murdered – and her family have warned Britain’s prison system is “not fit for purpose”.



Kendall, who had 47 previous convictions across 78 offences, had been jailed for assaulting Michaela but was wrongly classified as a “medium risk” offender on his release and was allowed to move back in to the house with no close monitoring.

A probation report had failed to include crucial details about his previous violence towards the 49-year-old mum — including an incident in which he had strangled her.

It meant Kendall was released under less stringent conditions than if he had been correctly deemed high risk and was able to return to Michaela’s home in Mount Hawke, Cornwall.



Just two weeks later, on May 31, 2021, he murdered her by stabbing her in the eye with a kitchen knife following a row over a meal she had made him.

Now Shaun, 18, and his grandfather Peter Hall, 74, fear other families could suffer the same fate if thousands of prisoners are released early into an already overstretched probation system.

Shaun said: “What I remember is he was labelled as a medium risk and he should have been labelled a high risk.

“It was a disaster.”

Shaun claimed the probation officer who took on Kendall’s case “shouldn’t have dealt with it”.



He explained: “She forgot to include important details to the judge and so it all went down a different channel.

“If he had been properly assessed, he would have been dealt with very differently on his release.

“That mistake set in motion a whole different tragic set of events.



“He ended up being released under a set of circumstances he shouldn’t have – it was catastrophic.”

Shaun, who is now taking legal action against the police and probation service, believes his mum could still be alive if Kendall had been correctly assessed.

He said: “If he was properly categorised as a high risk, he wouldn’t have been released [in the same circumstances] and the extra restrictions could have kept him away.

“That was another opportunity to prevent this.”

His grandfather Peter is now questioning how authorities will safely assess thousands more offenders being released from prison.



The government are set to release 5,000 offenders from October in a bid to free up space in overcrowded jails.

Critics have however warned the probation service may not be able to keep up with the demand of monitoring offenders.

He said: “Five years ago they failed Michaela. There is no evidence anything has improved. What I see is it has got worse.

“The problem we have got now is this is the same probation service letting 5,000 prisoners go. Who is making that assessment?

“Out of those 5,000, who is making the call whether they are medium or high risk – especially those who have been involved in domestic violence?”



Peter believes the failures surrounding Kendall’s release demonstrate the potentially devastating consequences of getting those decisions wrong.

He said: “The severity of the mistakes they had made mean they are not fit for purpose.

“It is systemic. From the very top of the probation service. Right from the start when Lee Kendall was released from prison.

“He was assessed by someone not qualified to assess him. The report for him to be released was not complete.

“He had tried to strangle her but there was no mention of that. The judge did not have all the facts.”



Peter said that if Kendall had been correctly assessed as high risk, authorities could have imposed greater restrictions and monitored him more closely after he left prison.

Instead, he says, Kendall returned to Michaela.

Peter added: “When they released him, the police were supposed to have done a check and asked if she wanted him back to live with her – they didn’t.

“He went straight back to her house in Cornwall. He should have stayed in Plymouth.

“He should never have been released [in those circumstances], let alone back to her house. There should have been a ban on that and they should have checked on him.



“So many mistakes were made and he should have been recalled — but nobody bothered to call him out.”

Michaela met Kendall while working for a group helping freed convicts.

But she broke professional boundaries and began a sexual relationship, moving him into her home in Mount Hawke, Cornwall.

Michaela was soon subjected to numerous assaults by Kendall.

He was in and out of prison during their two-year relationship and was well known to police.



Authorities had recorded 16 assaults by him against her.

Shaun remembers growing increasingly uncomfortable around Kendall as a child and witnessing some of the abuse his mum endured.

He said: “He was drunk a lot of the time and I witnessed some of the domestic abuse.

“I did not fully understand domestic abuse. I knew what was happening but I did not know how I was meant to deal with it or what I was meant to do.

“It was a very manipulative relationship. He exerted a lot of control without her realising.



“It was not just physical but there was a lot of mental abuse and mind games.”

Seven months before Michaela’s death, Shaun moved out of the family home to stay with his aunt – something he now believes his mum arranged to protect him from Kendall.

He said: “I think Mum was trying to protect me from everything.

“There was a lot of stress with police and social services – and I think she just wanted to know I was safe.

“I see now she was trying to help him – fix him, I guess. Her knowing I was safe at my aunt’s allowed her to try and help him.”



On the night Michaela was killed, Kendall had drunk five bottles of wine before becoming angry over a dinner he “didn’t want”, Truro Crown Court previously heard.

Police were called to Michaela’s home but did not enter the property.

Body-worn camera footage later revealed one officer telling the control room they had visions of “her lying there with him covering her mouth”.

Shaun claims an officer also said his mum “didn’t help herself”.

He said: “The night she was killed police came to the house but did nothing.



“The police said she ‘didn’t help herself’. How can you say that to a victim of domestic abuse?

“She was trapped in the relationship and wanted help.

“Yet they just left her there without doing anything – and hours later she was dead.”



Michaela was eventually found dead by her father the following evening.

At an inquest in 2024, coroner Andrew Cox found there had been “shortcomings and errors” by probation services before her death.

Kendall was jailed for life for Michaela’s murder and ordered to serve a minimum of 21 years.

Now 18, Shaun says learning the full extent of what happened to his mum has made him determined to force change.

He said: “My mum was failed terribly by the police and probation service. We need change to stop this from happening again.



“The probation failed by classifying him as medium risk – he should have been high risk considering his past.

“There were obviously multiple incidents when he could and should have gone back to prison.

“No one made that call. It always felt a bit lazy just to let him back out and wait for something bigger to happen to then lock him away for a longer time.

“That obviously did happen – but the result of that was my mum lost her life.”

Before meeting Kendall in 2019, Shaun remembers a happy childhood with his mum and brother, spending days together at the beach.

He said: “She was always very loving. She was a wonderful mum and always made us feel comfortable.

“She was very caring to everyone, close friends and family, and would always look out for everyone.

“Getting involved in that relationship was really out of character for her. But there is not really a certain type of person it happens to.

“No one who knew her thought she would ever get into the situation and it shows it can happen to anyone.”



Shaun says he has needed therapy to process his mum’s murder and struggles with knowing she will miss the milestones of his adult life.

But rather than focus on Kendall, he wants his mum’s death to force changes in how dangerous offenders are handled.

He said: “The more I find out about how drastically the police and probation service failed my mum, the more determined I am.

“This could have been prevented on so many occasions.

“He should not have been able to have had that opportunity to take her life. He should have been shut off a long time ago.”



Peter said families of domestic abuse victims will understandably be terrified at the prospect of offenders being released early if the probation system cannot properly assess and monitor them.

He said: “There will be an awful lot of women and men who have been victims of domestic violence offenders potentially being released early who will be very anxious about what happens now.

“Michaela’s case was coercive behaviour and in these cases the offenders control their victims. They remove them from their families, isolate them.

“The families will have got some of those people back but soon could lose that when the perpetrators are released.”

Shaun and his family are now working with the Good Law Project and taking legal action against the police and probation service.



Shaun added: “We have no option but to go down the legal route.

“It is so important we stop this from happening again.”

The Ministry of Justice said Michaela’s murder was a “horrific crime” but it would be “inappropriate to comment on live legal proceedings”.

Jim Colwell, Deputy Chief Constable for Devon and Cornwall Police, said the force “immediately addressed recommendations made by the Independent Office for Police Conduct”.

He added: “We recognised some areas of learning in formal admissions within the inquest which have been implemented, and this work continues.”



Cat Knight, solicitor at the Good Law Project, said: “With one woman killed in the UK every three days, Michaela’s tragedy is all too common.

“The criminal justice system is failing women and putting them in danger.

“It’s time for the police and probation service to treat domestic abuse as a threat to life and tackle it with the urgency it demands.” of these prisoners – and we need to make sure they are held accountable.”

A Ministry of Justice spokesperson said: “The murder of Michaela Hall was a horrific crime, and our thoughts remain with her loved ones.

“We have always stated we wanted to go further to protect the public, and we are fast-tracking a plan to keep more of the most dangerous offenders behind bars. That’s on top of murderers, anyone on life sentences and those in prison for rape, serious child sexual abuse and grooming offences who are already blocked from any changes.



“Our record £700 million investment in probation is ensuring staff have the resources, powers and technology they need to manage offenders safely in the community, and we are tagging a record number of offenders to track their every move alongside investing a record £550m in victim support.”

News.title: Will there be a heatwave in September? When Met Office predicts hot UK weather will return after rain this week
News.content:
THE hot weather is set to return again this summer, according to the Met Office.

But sun-seekers are set to face a soaking first, with rain and thunderstorms sweeping across the country this week.



Will there be a heatwave in September?

The Met Office has raised the possibility of another heatwave between August 31 and September 14.

Its long-range forecast says temperatures are likely to be above average overall, with high pressure settling close to the south of the UK.



The Met Office said: “As we move into the start of meteorological autumn, signals for the prevailing weather patterns affecting the UK are weak, thus something close to the climatological norm is most likely.

“This means a broad northwest-southeast split in conditions, with the high pressure becoming centred close to the south of the UK and more changeable conditions developing towards the north and northwest.



“Meanwhile, drier, more settled weather is slightly more likely towards the south and east. Temperatures are likely to be above average overall.

“There is a chance that late season hot spells or heatwaves develop, especially in the south.”

It would follow the fifth heatwave of a record-breaking summer, which brought highs of 38.1C in Kew Gardens, London, on Thursday last week – the hottest day of the year so far.

Before then, a fairly unsettled spell is forecast from August 21 to 30, with showers and longer bursts of rain reaching many parts of the UK.



Drier breaks are expected too, with high pressure crossing the country at times.

Deeper Atlantic lows could also bring spells of widespread rain and strong winds, along with the odd thunderstorm.

Temperatures are predicted be above average, but the chance of “widespread or exceptional heat” seems less likely than in recent weeks.

When will it rain this week?

According to the Met Office, the north will be cloudy with outbreaks of rain today, turning heavier and more persistent across Northern Ireland and western Scotland this afternoon.

Further south, hazy sunshine is forecast to develop and it will be very warm and humid.



Rain pushes into northern England and North Wales by dawn, while the south is predicted to stay dry with clear spells and a slightly cooler night.

Tuesday should see a wet start across northern and central areas, with “rain moving erratically southwards” as the day goes on with brighter and fresher conditions sweeping in from the north.

Wednesday should be dry in the south, with a mix of sunshine and showers elsewhere.

But from Thursday the rain is forecast to become heavier and more widespread and there could be thunder.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Met Office meteorologist Tom Morgan said: “I can’t promise rain for all of us through the week ahead, but in the south at least, it’s looking like the most changeable week we’ve seen here, well at least since the end of June.”



He added that a jet stream to the north of the UK allowed high pressure to dominate, which caused the recent excessive heat, but it is now travelling southwards.

News.title: Hippo from Pablo Escobar's herd spotted prowling near school as urgent hunt launched
News.content:
Hippo from Pablo Escobar's herd spotted prowling near school as urgent hunt launched

The hippo was spotted walking freely through a quiet neighbourhood in Colombia, with locals watching on as it roamed near a school and approached a home

View 3 Images Shocked residents watched on as the hippo approached a home (Image: Jam Press)

A giant hippo from Pablo Escobar's infamous herd has been spotted roaming near a school, sparking fears for children and alarm amongst residents.

‌



The huge animal was seen wandering freely through a quiet neighbourhood on August 10, with locals watching on as it made its way through the streets and even approached a home.

‌



The shocking sighting unfolded in the El Limonar neighbourhood of Barrancabermeja, Colombia, with one resident filming the hippo as it wandered through the area.

‌



Environment department officials went to the scene to investigate and found tracks showing where the animal had travelled. They believe the hippo entered the neighbourhood through the La Lira creek, apparently emerging from a nearby wetland.

View 3 Images The hippo roamed near a school and approached a home in the El Limonar neighbourhood (Image: Jam Press)

The animal is part of a population that began after notorious drug lord Escobar brought several hippos to his private estate in Colombia in the 1980s. The animals have since multiplied to more than 200 and spread beyond the area where they were originally kept.

‌



Leonardo Granados, the city's Environment Secretary, said a local resident had watched the animal emerge from the area.

He said: "According to the testimony of the young man who was able to observe from this window that the hippo came out, this is where it entered.

"Here are the tracks showing that it flattened all the vegetation, came out, went around that area and then went back in."

‌



The area is now being scoured by vets, biologists and Environmental Police officers in an attempt to locate the animal and establish the route it took.

Authorities are also looking into the possibility it could be the same hippo previously spotted at least three times in rural areas of the municipality.

Granados said the district would work to implement risk-prevention protocols relating to invasive species that could pose a danger to residents. The aim would be to capture the animal and relocate it away from Barrancabermeja.

‌



View 3 Images Pablo Escobar brought several hippos to his private estate in Colombia in the 1980s (Image: Jam Press)

Since January this year, the district has reportedly submitted more than 20 requests to Colombia’s Ministry of Environment and Regional Autonomous Corporations over the presence of hippos in the city.

Several sightings have been reported in Barrancabermeja this year, increasing concerns about the animals venturing into populated areas.

Article continues below

"We are concerned about the safety of children; we are concerned about the safety of families," Granados said. "We are here talking right next to this house; it is already in the urban area."

Authorities have proposed installing camera traps with the Jaguar Foundation to monitor the animal's movements and establish where it is travelling. It remains unclear whether the hippo is the same one seen elsewhere in the department in previous sightings.

Authorities have urged anyone who spots a hippo not to approach it and to immediately report the sighting to the National Police or Environment Department.

News.title: Mum of boy, 5, who plunged to death from 15th floor flat says council 'failed' her
News.content:
Mum of boy, 5, who plunged to death from 15th floor flat says council 'failed' her

Five-year-old Aalim Ahmed died after falling from the kitchen window of his family's flat in Plaistow, east London in May 2024

View 3 Images Aalim Ahmed fell from a 15th-floor flat in east London (Image: Getty Images)

A grieving mum has told an inquest her five-year-old son's death was “preventable”, saying he “could have been here” if the council had acted on her safety concerns.

Aalim Ahmed died after falling from the kitchen window of his family's 15th floor home at Jacobs House in Plaistow, east London, on May 16 2024. His father found him on a railing below the block shortly before 6am.

His mother Sahra Osman told Walthamstow Coroner's Court she had repeatedly raised concerns with Newham Council about the safety of the windows before her son's death.

She said Aalim had autism and “no sense of danger”, and believed he may have climbed up while trying to reach a biscuit from a cupboard. Ms Osman claimed the safety restrictors on the windows did not work properly and that repeated visits by workmen failed to resolve the problem.

View 3 Images The incident occurred in May 2024 (Image: PA)

Giving evidence, she became emotional and said: “I did everything I could as a mum to protect my son.” The family had moved into the top-floor property in February 2023, when Ms Osman was heavily pregnant with a daughter. She told the court she had felt “scared” and “horrified” about moving into the flat, which needed repairs, and did not believe it was suitable for her family.

She told the court she had been advised to accept the property and raise her concerns afterwards rather than risk becoming homeless by refusing it.

Ms Osman said she continued raising concerns about the windows after moving in. The court heard she had also informed the council of Aalim's autism diagnosis by email.

She said she believed she had sent a further letter about his condition. People who knew Aalim had also sent a letter to the council saying the family needed to be moved because they were not safe, the inquest heard.

Ms Osman told Sandesh Singh, representing Newham Council: “You guys could have prevented this tragic thing from happening. If you had done your job, he could have been here.

“I think that Newham Council failed me as a mum, as a tenant.

“I tried everything. I tried to tell them my concerns about safety multiple times and you guys ignored me rather than doing anything about the actual issues.”

She added: “I told you my son (Aalim) has autism.

“I do not know what more I can prove. I showed you a GP letter. The people that knew him sent a letter to the council saying this family need to be moved from this flat because they are not safe.”

The inquest heard that an engineer visited the property in January 2024. Ms Osman said she tried the windows during the visit and was still able to open them.

She wanted restrictors fitted to every window and said one bedroom window could be left “just open wide”, which left her feeling “quite scared”.

The engineer said he would look into getting the problem fixed, but Ms Osman said that within a day she found a window restrictor on the floor.

She contacted the council again and said she begged for help and asked to speak to a manager, telling the inquest: “The window was wide open, it would not lock, it was hanging.”

Ms Osman said she made clear that she believed the problem posed a danger to her children, but claimed it was not treated as an emergency. She told the hearing: “The restrictors were not working, they were there for decoration.”

View 3 Images Aalim's father found him on a railing below the block shortly before 6am (Image: PA)

Ms Osman also said she became frustrated as it could take months to receive a proper response from the council. During questioning, the council suggested an engineer had been told about an issue in the living room but not with the kitchen window restrictor.

‌



Ms Osman disputed this and maintained she had raised concerns about windows throughout the property, accusing the council of “not taking my situation seriously enough”.

She also rejected a suggestion that she may have forced a window open during hot weather.

Ms Osman said all the windows were always closed before the family went to bed. On the morning Aalim died, her toddler began shouting “Aalim”, “window” and “outside”, alerting the family that something was wrong.

‌



Ms Osman said her partner went to the kitchen window and was “just crying and screaming in shock” after seeing his son's pyjamas below.

Aalim's father, Makail Ahmed, described the moment as one of “disbelief – it was a nightmare.” He ran downstairs and found his son, while neighbours who had been woken by the noise called 999.

The inquest has previously heard that Aalim was identified by his family and that his cause of death was multiple injuries caused by trauma from a “fall from height”.

Article continues below

Assistant coroner Ian Wade said at the start of proceedings: “One of the things I bear in mind is the horrendous loss borne by Aalim’s family and indeed the community.

“I am very conscious that this should never have happened but how it happened remains to be seen.”

The hearing continues.

News.title: Busted's James Bourne makes first public outing after surgery to 'extend life'
News.content:
Busted's James Bourne makes first public outing after surgery to 'extend life'

Busted star James Bourne, who had to quit the bands tour over his ill health, has been seen out and out amid his mystery illness, just weeks after sharing an update

View 4 Images Busted star James Bourne has made a rare public outing amid his mystery illness (Image: Instagram/disvicious1)

James Bourne has made a rare public outing amid his mystery illness. The singer, 42, who is best known as a member of Busted alongside Matt Willis and Charlie Simpson, had to quit the band's tour with McFly last year and later revealed that he was suffering from poor health.

‌



He has been relatively quiet about his illness and has been seen very little since he made the announcement, but, on Monday, a post on social media which showed him enjoying time with friends.

‌



Guitarist Tommy Henriksen works with Alice Cooper and Johnny Depp's supergroup Hollywood Vampires and a snap appeared on his Instagram Story after the band played in Scarborough over the weekend. A caption on the post read: "My UK friends."

‌



4 View 4 Images James has not publicly disclosed his illness but did say that the underwent surgery to extend his life (Image: Getty Images For Bauer Media) 4 View 4 Images James had to pull out of Busted's tour with McFly last year (Image: Getty Images)

In the photo, James can be seen looking in good spirits, wearing a white T-shirt and a black hoodie slung over his shoulder. James has not disclosed the exact nature of his illness, but did previously say he had undergone surgery to extend his life.

Towards the end of last month, James took to social media to share a rare update, thanking fans for their ongoing support. He wrote: "As I’m taking a break from the gram, I’ll be posting an update soon about what’s going on with my health in my Spotify bio. It’s a long story. Still not out of the woods yet. Thanks for your support and patience."

‌



James issued a statement previously where he said he needed surgery to extend his life. Writing on his Instagram Stories, he wrote: "I realised it's been about six months since I posted last.

View 4 Images Busted shot to fame in the early 2000s and became known for hits like What I Go To School For and Year 3000 (Image: Getty Images)

"I have a plan in place to have a major surgery that should extend my life and hopefully make me well enough to come back to what I love the most, which is touring and making music. It really sucks to be out of the game. But there is hope!"

‌



James shocked his fans when he announced he'd be stepping down from the McFly Vs Busted tour last year owing to his poor health. He said he would miss being there but had to put his health first.

"The VS tour kicks off tomorrow night in Birmingham and as excited as l've been all year for this tour to begin, I'm really sorry to say that over the last 8 days it has become clear that I am not in good enough health to play these shows," he said at the time.

"There's a lot of information I still don't have about my condition but my bandmates, management and I are unanimous in deciding that I should focus on the medical stuff for now.

Article continues below

"I really hope I can be in a position to come back further down the line. It's still going to. be an amazing show and I will miss being there! See you all as soon as possible."

News.title: Richard Tice blasted over 'insulting' heatwave comment as he says Brits should celebrate
News.content:
Richard Tice blasted over 'insulting' heatwave comment as he says Brits should celebrate

Nigel Farage's number two, Richard Tice, was blasted after claiming Brits should celebrate soaring temperatures as they make sparkling wine better - despite hundreds of people dying and homes being burned in wildfires

View 4 Images Richard Tice has come under fire over his remarks about the heatwave (Image: PA)

Nigel Farage's number two has been blasted after dismissing the misery caused by the heatwave - which claimed hundreds of lives - and said Brits should enjoy sparkling wine instead.

‌



Richard Tice's remarks were branded an insult to those affected after he hit out at the "doom and gloom" around climate change and urged people to celebrate soaring temperatures instead. Huge wildfires have raged in recent days, with people forced from their homes in worst-affected areas including Stourbridge in the West Midlands.

‌



And the Met Office estimates 2,700 people died from heat-related causes in the May and June heatwaves alone - with 42% of these fatalities a result of "human-induced warming".

‌



Reform UK deputy leader Mr Tice sparked anger after telling a press conference in Westminster: "Climate change has always happened, it always will. Maybe the smarter thing to do is to adapt to it, (rather) than think arrogantly you can stop it.

Reform UK accused of 'punishing' people who most need welfare system with draconian plan READ MORE :

View 4 Images The aftermath of devastating wildfires in Stourbridge on Monday (Image: Joe Giddens/PA Wire)

"I'm old enough to remember 1976 - this feels a bit the same. That was 50 years ago. I think when it's a bit warm, let's enjoy it. And if it means that English wine and sparkling wine gets better and better, fantastic.

‌



"That means we can take on the French, fantastic. Let's celebrate some of these things rather than just be sort of doom and gloom about it."

The heatwaves have taken a huge toll on the UK economy, analysis suggests. Thinktank Verdant estimated that so far the country has taken a £4.4billion hit this year alone due to the weather's impact on business output.

On a visit to Stourbridge on Monday, Housing Secretary Angela Rayner voiced her horror at the devastation. She told The Mirror: "It was like going through a movie. I've never seen that level of devastation and the indiscriminate way in which you can see the fire had moved so swiftly."

‌



Mr Tice's comments provoked a furious response from environmental groups. Danny Gross, climate campaigner at Friends of the Earth, said: “If Richard Tice wants to live in a world of make believe, that’s his call. But telling people to enjoy the heat after the scenes we’ve seen in the last week… how out of touch do you need to be?

“Homes burnt to a cinder and the military drafted in after wildfires raged uncontrollably. Farmers at their wits end because weeks without rain have made for yet another brutal harvest.

"And the more than 1,000 lives needlessly lost during this summer’s heatwaves thanks to global heating. It’s an insult - particularly to their loved ones - to suggest the weather extremes we’re seeing are cause for celebration."

‌



View 4 Images Huge wildfires have blighted the UK in recent days (Image: sky)

He pointed to Friends of the Earth polling which found 87% of people think the UK is unprepared for extreme weather events like heat and drought. This includes 81% of Reform UK supporters.

Mr Gross added: "Failing to acknowledge the real-world consequences of our changing climate may not be as easily forgiven as he thinks."

‌



Amy Cameron, a programme director for Greenpeace UK, said: “Tice’s words show that a party bankrolled by fossil fuel interests will keep denying the climate crisis for its funders’ benefit even when its impacts are undeniable.

"Reform should try telling nurses fainting on shifts, farmers losing their crops and people running from burning homes to enjoy the hot weather and see what reaction they’ll get.

"There's only one way to stop this extreme weather: cutting emissions from fossil fuels. Things will only get from bad to worse if we listen to the politicians being paid to deny it's even happening."

‌



View 4 Images More than a doezn properties were destroyed in Stourbridge (Image: Anadolu via Getty Images)

And Alasdair Johnstone, from the Energy and Climate Intelligence Unit, said: “Far from being an enjoyable experience, for many this summer will have brought hardship, with 2,877 deaths during the May and June heatwaves, over 1,100 of which are directly attributable to the extra heat added by climate change.

"Firefighters have been called to over 1,000 wildfires, which have devastated the landscape, displaced people, and destroyed home. The only way these climate change impacts can be prevented from becoming more common and severe is to tackle the cause, which means reaching net zero emissions by 2050.”

‌



Mr Tice is a long-term critic of the government's Net Zero drive, which aims to cut atmosphere-warming emissions to effectively zero by 2050. Green Party MP Hannah Spencer told The Mirror: "This is a load of rubbish- and not surprising to hear from the party who is funded by fossil fuel billionaires.

"As one of the wealthier people in the country, of course Richard Tice is not worried because he's not going to be affected in the same way everyone else will. The threat to our own security, from food, energy to people's health is already happening and will only get worse.

"The Green Party would be very happy to invite Richard Tice to talk to us and other experts on the dangers of the climate emergency. He could also try talking to his own voters, I've certainly spoken to a lot of them, and a large majority of them really care about the planet and support tougher action on climate."

News.title: Helicopter crashes in Sifnos leaving three dead and sparking major fire
News.content:
Helicopter crashes in Sifnos leaving three dead and sparking major fire

The helicopter went down and sparked a fire in the Tholos neighbourhood on the popular Greek tourist island of Sifnos, with three bodies recovered from the site

View 2 Images Three people have died after a helicopter crashed in Greece

Three people have been killed in a helicopter crash which sparked a huge fire on the popular Greek tourist island of Sifnos.

The private helicopter went down shortly after 6pm local time today (4pm UK time).

Rescue crews and firefighters raced to the crash site close to homes in the Tholos neighbourhood and quickly brought the flames under control.

The bodies of three people were recovered from the site, the fire department said. The identities of those on board and the cause of the crash have not yet been confirmed.

Emergency services were first alerted to the incident at around 6:17pm, reports Proto Thema.

View 2 Images Sifnos is a popular island in the western Aegean Sea (Image: Getty Images)

Firefighters attended the scene alongside a rescue team from Syros, which arrived on a high-speed boat operated by the Fire Brigade.

An image taken in the immediate aftermath appeared to show thick black smoke billowing from a fireball at the crash site.

Sifnos is a stunning island in the western part of the Cyclades island group in Greece, sitting right between Serifos and Milos.

It sits around 76 nautical miles (140 km) from Athens' main port, Piraeus, and is widely celebrated as a culinary hotspot with a rich pottery history and scenic villages.
