The lack of European football has prompted a major strategy shift from Blues transfer chiefs, who have traded in their policy of buying young by adding old heads Danny Welbeck and Jordan Henderson to the ranks of Xabi Alonso‘s squad this season.

They start their season with a trip down to road to Fulham next Monday.

Sports.title: Referee Urs Meier reveals he DIDN’T SEE foul in Sol Campbell’s England goal vs Portugal despite disallowing it Euro 2004
Sports.content:
IT might have been 22 years since it happened, but England won’t forget – or forgive – the refereeing decision that knocked them out of Euro 2004.

Of course, it takes a lot more than one decision to knock a country out of a tournament. But, when Sol Campbell scored a towering header in the 90th minute, the Three Lions thought they had moved on to the semi-finals.



Instead, Swiss referee Urs Meier chalked the goal off on his own accord. This was way before VAR could take the brunt of the fall.

The tie then went to extra time and penalties where first David Beckham and then Darius Vassell would miss to bring their tournament to an end.



Worse still, Portugal went all the way to the final and lost to surprise package Greece.

Meier has since said his gut screamed “foul” when Campbell scored.



Even if he hadn’t seen a foul himself, he felt something wrong. Thus, he disallowed the goal.

Only later, watching the replays, did Meier notice the Portuguese goalkeeper’s arms were not raised to catch the ball.

John Terry, who jumped alongside Campbell, had made some contact with the goalkeeper. That was the foul Meier believed he saw.

Meier still proudly stands by that call: “It didn’t feel right,” he said of the goal. “With experience, I learned to trust that feeling.”



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

Campbell, naturally, has a very different opinion.

In the wake of the exit in 2004, the England defender said: “I believe if it was the other way round it would have been a goal to the Portuguese.

“Having seen it now, I’m even more convinced that it was a goal.

“The worst moment for me wasn’t Darius’ or David’s miss in the penalty shoot-out, it was that goal being disallowed because it shouldn’t have gone as far as a penalty shoot-out.”



Another in a long line of ‘what ifs’ for England.

Sports.title: Georgina Rodriguez shares video revealing ‘how my husband wakes me up’ after marrying Cristiano Ronaldo
Sports.content:
GEORGINA RODRIGUEZ has shared a video on social media revealing how Cristiano Ronaldo ‘wakes me up’.

The Argentine-Spanish model married the footballing superstar on August 11 at a stunning £30million mansion following a 10-year relationship.



They shared a joint Instagram post following the private ceremony announcing they tied the knot and showing off their lavish rings.

And Georgina has wasted no time in flaunting the new name she can now call her hubby.



Taking to Instagram, the 32-year-old posted a clip of Ronaldo doing some lengths in a swimming pool on a scorching 45C day in their home in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia.

She captioned the post: “This is how my husband wakes me up.”

Fans took to the comments to joke how she has been waiting for to call the 41-year-old her husband.

One said: “Georgina was waiting for these moments to call the Goat her husband officially.”

A second said: “Sis couldn’t wait to use ‘My husband’.”

Another said: “‘My husband’ mommy win.”



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

A fourth added: “‘Husband’ love the sound of that.”

The pair’s five children – two of whom are biologically Georgina’s – were all in attendance at their wedding.

The civil ceremony in Cascais, Portugal, was described as ‘private and intimate’ by the Daily Mail.

But Ronaldo’s doting mum Dolores Aveiro and his three siblings Hugo, Elma and Katia, were NOT present at the intimate civil ceremony as they married in front of just four witnesses and their children.

Sports.title: Real paid £120m for Diomande, City want £85m for Savinho… Chelsea eyeing £100m for Pedro Neto doesn’t seem so bad now
Sports.content:
CHELSEA have set an asking price of close to £100m for any club interested in signing Pedro Neto this summer.

A rip-off, right? Wrong.



With a range of suitors for Neto, 26, including Manchester City and beyond, the Blues heavy asking price will certainly be enough to put some clubs off.

And while no formal bids have been put to the Stamford Bridge outfit for Neto, he has been strongly linked to Saudi side Al-Hilal this week.



The asking price at first glance seems astronomical for a winger who put up five Premier League goals and six assists last term.

But in the context of this transfer window, it’s not so bad, with Manchester City holding out for £85m for Savinho, who racked up one goal and two assists in the same time period.



Yan Diomande joined Real Madrid from RB Leipzig for a fee worth up to £120m, while Bradley Barcola is valued at more than £100m by PSG amid links to Liverpool this window.

When you hear those figures, £100m for Neto seems a little more reasonable.

And while they would sell him for the right price, as with many players, Chelsea are not actively looking to sell the player who was their best performing winger last season.

He is highly appreciated internally, which is proven by the fact he started in their final friendly of pre-season, a win over Real Sociedad, but also reflected by the price tag set for his move.



BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

With Morgan Rogers signing, and Cole Palmer expected to drift in more from the right under Xabi Alonso, Neto’s position in the team has been questioned.

But it seems Alonso has a plan to make use of him as a wingback, which he did in Saturday’s 3-1 win, with it being Neto’s cross that was headed by Joao Pedro before Rogers tapped home the opener.

He also featured in pre-season in a 4-2-3-1 system, in which he played more as an out and out winger, sharing minutes with Estevao, who that position perhaps suits a little more given his directness and Neto’s engine to defend as well as attack.

There have been reports that Neto has agreed personal terms with Saudi side Al-Hilal, though those are unconfirmed.



He is not the only player linked with a move away from the club, with Blues chiefs setting a price tag for plenty of other assets that could be gone before the window closes.

Among those are Enzo Fernandez for £120m, Nicolas Jackson for £65m, and Liam Delap for £50m.

But they are not alone in being up for grabs, with more than 35 ‘first-team’ players still registered to the Blues for this season, with only 18 available to be named in any given matchday squad.

Sports.title: Forgotten Chelsea winger Diego Moreira ‘agrees £47.5m transfer to Ruben Amorim’s AC Milan’ after being sold for £1.7m
Sports.content:
EX-CHELSEA player Diego Moreira has reportedly agreed a stunning £47.5MILLION move to AC Milan.

The former Blues winger, 22, is set to join Ruben Amorim’s side from sister club Strasbourg in a huge deal.



Transfer guru Fabrizio Romano claims Milan have reached a verbal agreement worth £43m plus add-ons, which could take the package to around £47.5m.

A sell-on clause is also understood to have been included, with paperwork now being prepared ahead of the switch.



Romano added that Moreira only wanted to join Milan despite receiving approaches from clubs in Germany and England.

The staggering transfer comes just two years after Chelsea sold the Belgian international, who made only a single appearance for the club, to Strasbourg for just £1.7m.



Moreira had joined the Blues from Benfica on a free transfer in 2023 but struggled to make an impact at Stamford Bridge.

He made just one senior appearance for Chelsea, coming off the bench in a Carabao Cup win over AFC Wimbledon, and also spent time on loan at Lyon.

Moreira was then shipped to Strasbourg in 2024, where he rebuilt his career and established himself as a highly-rated attacking talent.

His rise has now convinced Milan to splash out on the versatile wide man as Amorim continues reshaping his squad at the San Siro.

Sports.title: Aston Villa Dream Team preview: top stars, smart options & potential flops
Sports.content:
ASTON VILLA stumbled out of the blocks last season but rallied to finish fourth while also going all the way in the Europa League.

The Villains have sold Morgan Rogers, Lucas Digne and Youri Tielemans this summer but Dream Team managers know not to underestimate them while Unai Emery is at the helm.

PLAY DREAM TEAM NOW: £100,000 PRIZE POT!



Ahead Gameweek 1, we’ve analysed Villa’s top stars, smart options and potential flops.



TOP STARS

Ollie Watkins (£5m) is a proven Premier League performer having scored 15+ goals in each of his last four top flight campaigns.

Last season, he finished strong to end with 21 goals in all competitions — Erling Haaland (£8.5m) and Igor Thiago (£4.5m) were the only strikers who amassed superior tallies.

Ezri Konsa (£4m) was one of the only three defenders to achieve 50+ bonus points in 2025/26.

The England centre-back is a reliable performer who is guaranteed to play every minute that matters if he’s available for selection.

It’s worth noting that both Konsa and Watkins started their pre-season training late after going deep at the World Cup with the Three Lions but that is unlikely to be a major concern as they are ultra important players.

It might be overly zealous to name Johan Manzambi (£4m) as one of Villa’s top stars given he is yet to play a single minute in claret and blue but he’s a tremendous prospect.

The 20-year-old starred for Switzerland at the World Cup and is likely to be tasked with filling Rogers’ boots.



Categorised as a midfielder, Manzambi has occasionally been effective as a second striker.

At this stage, the talented youngster is considered a doubt for Gameweek 1 but gaffers should monitor his progress closely.

SMART OPTIONS

Come Christmas, Dream Team bosses might be chuckling about the fact Brian Madjo (£2.5m) started the season at such an affordable price.

The 17-year-old striker produced a highly impressive performance against PSG in the Super Cup, including a well-taken volley just before half time.



Despite his tender age, the hulking 6ft 4in forward looks ready for Premier League action and it will be interesting to see how Emery uses him, though he’s considered a doubt for August’s fixtures at this stage.

Digne’s departure means Ian Maatsen (£3.5m) is now first-choice left-back.

The Dutchman wasn’t viable last term because he was a minutes risk but that problem appears to be solved.

At £3.5m he’s a tad cheaper than Konsa and Matty Cash (£4m), which makes him a useful alternative.

Elsewhere, Emi Buendia (£3.5m) is attractively priced for a midfielder who notched 11 goals and nine assists last season, averaging a goal involvement every 144.3 minutes.



Villa’s No10 will be expected to step up now Rogers and Tielemans have departed.

Sports.title: Jack Grealish, 30, given hope of resurrecting Man City career as Enzo Maresca praises Community Shield display
Sports.content:
ENZO MARESCA has refused to guarantee Jack Grealish first-team football this season.

But he insists he WILL give the winger every chance to earn a spot in his starting XI.



Manchester City‘s £100million man was deemed surplus to requirements by Pep Guardiola last season and was fobbed off to Everton on loan.

Grealish, 30, showed glimpses of the form that prompted City to break the bank for his services, but his campaign ended with a whimper in January after he suffered a stress fracture in his left foot.



New City supremo Maresca threw the winger a bone in their Community Shield calamity against Arsenal last Sunday.

But he’s warned the England international he’ll warm the bench if he doesn’t rediscover his magic.



The Italian said: “Jack came on when we were already 2-0 down so the game had already become complicated. But overall, I think Jack was good.

“The ones that are still here are gonna work every day, and if they deserve it, they’re going to get minutes.”

Maresca is seemingly open to selling the former Aston Villa man should the right offer come in.

He added: “At the moment, the transfer window is open and we’ll see what happens.”



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

Grealish joined City from Villa in the summer of 2020, penning a five-year deal at the Etihad.

He’s made 158 appearances for the club, scoring 17 goals and providing 23 assists.

During his time at the Etihad, he’s won three Premier League titles, one Champions League and one FA Cup.

Man City kick off their Premier League campaign on Sunday, welcoming Bournemouth to Eastlands.

Sports.title: Karim Benzema ‘set to terminate £2million-a-WEEK Saudi contract with England star Ollie Watkins lined up as replacement’
Sports.content:
KARIM BENZEMA’s lucrative stay in Saudi Arabia could be coming to a close, according to reports, opening the door for Ollie Watkins to line his pockets.

Tensions are boiling over for Benzema at Al- Hilal – the second Saudi team he has played for after Al-Ittihad – and if the Frenchman is to leave, he is reportedly demanding that the final year of his £2million-a-WEEK wages are paid in full.



According to MaxiFoot, the Saudi giants are considering parting ways with the 38-year-old Frenchman in order to rejuvenate their squad.

But the 2022 Ballon d’Or winner will only accept if the final year of his deal is paid in full, and that is proving to be a stumbling block to his departure.



According to Spanish publication AS, Al- Hilal boss Simonee Inzaghi views Aston Villa forward Ollie Watkins as an ideal candidate to replace Benzema.

The 30-year-old netted 21 goals in 55 appearances for Villa during the 2025-26 campaign and his pace is a dimension Inzaghi wants to add to his attack.

Tensions between Benzema and his club surfaced during Al-Hilal’s 4-2 victory over Al- Faisaly on Friday evening.

Despite scoring earlier in the match, Benzema was visibly annoyed after being substituted 20 minutes from time for youngster Kader Meite.

Addressing the media after the match, Inzaghi sought to defuse the controversy surrounding his veteran star.

He said: “We talked about that after the match.



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

“It’s normal that he wants to play every match, and I understand him because I was a striker too.

“At that moment, we had another young player available, Kader Meite, who represents the future of the club. I was joking with Karim after the match, and I have a respectful relationship with him.

“He is not only a great champion, but also a very great professional.”

Watkins has two years left on his deal with Villa and has been the subject of interest from Arsenal in recent years.

Sports.title: Man Utd captain Fernandes not for sale despite Galatasaray interest
Sports.content:
Manchester United captain Bruno Fernandes is not for sale at any price despite interest from Galatasaray.

Reports have claimed the Turkish side are ready to bid for the 31-year-old, who has entered the final year of his contract, but United also have an option to extend by a further year.

However, United will not entertain any offers for their talisman, who was named Premier League Player of the Year last season after breaking the competition's assist record.

The £57m release clause for foreign clubs in his contract has now expired.

In December, Fernandes revealed he had been "hurt" when United told him last summer he was free to accept a big-money offer to join Saudi Arabian club Al Hilal, who were ready to pay £100m as a transfer fee.

Despite Fernandes feeling as though the club were open to selling him last summer, the message from the hierarchy since has been clear: he is not for sale.

The ambiguity of last summer has been put to bed with United viewing Fernandes as crucial to the future of their project.

Could Man Utd really sell Fernandes?

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Watch footage of Manchester United captain Bruno Fernandes returning to training ahead of a new Premier League season! X credit: @ManUtd.

Sky Sports' James Savundra on The Transfer Show:

"It doesn't seem likely in this window but go back 12 months, it felt 50:50. It felt like Manchester United would be willing to sell him if they could recoup £100m to spend on other areas.

"He spoke quite openly about the fact he spoke to the Saudi Pro League and the projects there - before deciding he wanted to commit his future to Manchester United.

"You would think the club would be working on a contract extension because he has one year left - plus that option to extend by a further year, which you'd expect them to do so, otherwise he'd be in a position in January where he could speak to foreign clubs over a free transfer.

"Last season he was just incredible with the assist record - he was the best player in the Premier League last season. He's a massive part of Michael Carrick's plans this season.

"There will come a time when Manchester United think about life after Bruno Fernandes but that won't be this summer. He's so important to their plans in Europe and the Premier League."

Image: Joshua Zirkzee has impressed for Manchester United in pre-season

Sky Sports' News' Danyal Khan:

"The good news for Michael Carrick and United is that two players, in particular, have stood out in pre-season.

"Having perhaps looked a bit tired towards the end of last season, Carrick will be purring to see Bryan Mbeumo and Amad Diallo back to their electric selves in pre-season.

"Mbeumo has looked sharp in front of goal with Amad also appearing full of confidence after an impressive World Cup with Cote d'Ivoire in the summer.

"One player who may have a new chapter at the club is Joshua Zirkzee. Although there is still a possibility his future could be away from Old Trafford, he's looked like a different Zirkzee to the one we've seen in previous seasons.

"Albeit it is pre-season, could Zirkzee provide cover for Fernandes in the No 10 position?

"He was particularly impressive in Dublin against Leeds at a sold-out Croke Park, and in his third season at the club it will be intriguing to see how Carrick uses the Dutchman - if his future is at United."

Sports.title: How are Man Utd shaping up ahead of the new season?
Sports.content:
Manchester United ended their pre-season with a 4-2 defeat to AC Milan, and the question is what kind of condition they are in as they go into the new season?

Ahead of a special Sky Sports Manchester United Q&A taking place on Wednesday, our reporter Danyal Khan discusses the major talking points...

Mbeumo, Amad look recharged - Zirkzee too?

The good news for Michael Carrick and United is that two players, in particular, have stood out in pre-season.

Having perhaps looked a bit tired towards the end of last season, Carrick will be purring to see Bryan Mbeumo and Amad Diallo back to their electric selves in pre-season.

Mbeumo has looked sharp in front of goal with Amad also appearing full of confidence after an impressive World Cup with Cote d'Ivoire in the summer.

One player who may have a new chapter at the club is Joshua Zirkzee. Although there is still a possibility his future could be away from Old Trafford, he's looked like a different Zirkzee to the one we've seen in previous seasons.

Image: Could Joshua Zirkzee play a crucial role for Manchester United this season?

Albeit it is pre-season, could Zirkzee provide cover for Bruno Fernandes in the No 10 position?

He was particularly impressive in Dublin against Leeds at a sold-out Croke Park, and in his third season at the club it will be intriguing to see how Carrick uses the Dutchman - if his future is at United.

Why they need a left-back

One thing that has clearly stood out in pre-season is the development of their gameplan under Carrick and his staff.

It was quite clear watching them during his six-month spell last season that the team would largely defend on the edge of their own box. They were extremely solid and compact which underpinned some huge wins.

What we've seen in pre-season has been a deviation - or, perhaps, progression - from that. United are pushing higher and working harder to press and counter-press the opposition, especially to win the ball back quickly after a loss of possession.

They were slightly found out against Milan, with the press not quite sharp enough - the fourth goal, in particular, came from just one ball over a high-lined defence.

Image: Manchester United collapsed against AC Milan

The game (although not wanting to exaggerate due to it still being pre-season!) was the perfect illustration of why United need to invest seriously in a left-back: not just because Luke Shaw will need to be rotated with the increased number of games that comes with European competition, but also due to the way United clearly want to play going forward.

They need serious recovery pace in the back-line for the times they do occasionally get caught out with this gameplan - but time is ticking to get any deal done.

Rashford - a topic that won't go away

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Watch the last goal Marcus Rashford scored for Manchester United before his loan spells at Aston Villa and Barcelona. Can he get back to scoring ways for the Red Devils?

Marcus Rashford has returned - and his future is a topic that will not go away until September's deadline passes.

It seemed an unlikely reunion after his loan spell at Barcelona, but from what I'm hearing Rashford has only been positive and enthusiastic about his return to the club.

Carrick also told us last week that Rashford is his player and he is looking forward to working with the forward going into the season, but there still seems to be doubt over whether the England man will remain in a United shirt.

Right now, he is expected to do so, but much will depend on the interest Rashford generates as the deadline approaches - and also what the player believes is right for his next challenge.

It is thought he would only leave for an elite-level club, but his current contact at United may mean it proves too difficult to organise a solution away from Old Trafford.

Sports.title: MCC Female Young Broadcaster of the Year joins Hundred final coverage
Sports.content:
The MCC Female Young Broadcaster of the Year for 2026, Rosa Simkin, received the ultimate competition prize when joining Sky Sports' live coverage of The Hundred final at Lord's on Sunday.

During the innings break of both the women's and men's finals, Rosa held flash interviews talking to Georgia Adams from Trent Rockets and Noor Ahmad from Manchester Super Giants as both teams ultimately went on to lift the titles.

The 18-year-old also presented some of the bitesize highlight videos for Sky Sports Cricket's digital channels and made content for Lord's Instagram, giving audiences an insight into her day as part of the team.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of The Hundred Women’s Final between Trent Rockets and SunRisers Leeds.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of the men's Hundred final between Trent Rockets and Manchester Super Giants at Lord's.

Prior to The Hundred, Rosa visited Sky's headquarters in Osterley for a look at broadcast production from behind the camera.

Here, she learned how cricket coverage is directed in studio, experienced various elements of live sport production, got a tour of the Sky Sports News studios and more.

She also met Jo Osborne, head of women's sport at Sky, for an invaluable chat about navigating the industry, before having a final preparation session with the cricket production team ahead of The Hundred final.

Now in its third year, the MCC Young Female Broadcaster competition, supported by Sky Sports and leading cricket charity Take Her Lead, aims to increase opportunities for young women aspiring to build a career in sports broadcasting, while uncovering and supporting the next generation of female broadcasting talent in cricket.

Image: Rosa Simkin poses with the Sky Sports cricket commentary team during The Hundred final at Lord's (image: Jed Leicester/ MCC)

The competition received 50 entries this year - its highest yet. The judging panel, including Sky Sports' director of cricket & NFL, Bryan Henderson, MCC chief marketing officer, Katie Maier, Take Her Lead founder and broadcaster, Isa Guha, as well as fellow broadcasters Alison Mitchell and Georgie Heath were hugely impressed by the standard of the showreel submissions and selected Rosa as the winner.

Rosa, a journalism student at Cardiff University, is from Warwickshire. She first fell in love with cricket at nine, when her sister Mae took her to Edgbaston to watch Warwickshire play.

She has held ECB media accreditation since the age of 16, having launched her platform, Rosa Talks Ball, while still at school. Since then, she has gone on to co-host and produce the weekly Two Tiers Deep podcast with Northamptonshire player Chloe Hill, exploring every level of the women's game, and founded TIERED, the first monthly magazine dedicated to women's county cricket.

Following her day broadcasting at The Hundred final, Rosa said: "Getting the chance to broadcast live on the field with the Sky Sports team was a truly incredible experience and one I won't forget.

"This competition with MCC, Sky Sports and Take Her Lead is already opening doors for me, from filming with Take Her Lead behind the scenes at Edgbaston and Trent Bridge and visiting Sky HQ, to media interviews, podcasts, and of course my ultimate prize at Lord's with the Sky Sports team.

"I can't wait to see where it takes me next in the broadcasting world!"

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Watch back the funniest and most memorable moments from this year's Hundred competition.

Bryan Henderson, director of cricket & NFL at Sky Sports, added: "Sky Sports was once again delighted to be involved in this brilliant initiative, and it was fantastic to see a record 50 entries this year showing just how important this competition is.

"The legacy over the three years has led to some very talented women establishing themselves in the sports broadcasting world.

"Rosa is a real talent, and we were proud to have her as part of our on-screen team for our coverage of The Hundred final."

Isa Guha, founder of Take Her Lead, said: "Rosa has shown real talent, curiosity and professionalism throughout the programme, and we have no doubt she has an incredibly bright future ahead.

"We look forward to continuing to support her on her broadcasting journey."

Sports.title: Alonso, Fernandez and a new era at Chelsea - podcast special!
Sports.content:
It's been another summer of change at Chelsea - and on the eve of a new Premier League season, there is so much to analyse at the club, with Xabi Alonso's reign kicking off, big-money transfers to be settled and a search for success on the pitch in their sights.

In a special Sky Sports podcast - A big summer for... Chelsea - Peter Smith is joined by Sky Sports News reporter James Savundra and Sky Sports football journalist David Richardson to discuss the key talking points at the club, including Enzo Fernandez's future amid interest from Manchester City and a £120m price tag.

The arrival of £117m Morgan Rogers and his partnership with Cole Palmer was also on the agenda, along with Alonso's new tactical set-up and the surprise signings of experienced pair Jordan Henderson and Danny Welbeck, which signalled a shift in the club's transfer policy.

Listen to the podcast below, watch it on the Sky Sports News YouTube channel or read on for the key points from the episode...

Enzo Fernandez - What's the latest?

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sky Sports News' James Savundra on whether Enzo Fernandez could still leave Stamford Bridge, despite Manchester City missing Chelsea's Friday 'deadline' last week

James Savundra: When I spoke to Xabi Alonso in his second week at work, he was glowing in his praise when it came to players like Reece James and Cole Palmer. But he gave very little away when it came to Enzo Fernandez. He only gave short sentences. The only thing he confirmed was that he was looking forward to working with him, and that he's a great player, but he didn't say much more than that, which made you think that, at that point, the saga [over Fernandez's future] hadn't been resolved.

I know that Fernandez has got a contract for another six years, but I think he wants to be better remunerated for what he offers to the side. As we know with the Chelsea contracts, some of them are very long, but they're more incentivised in terms of performance or if Chelsea go on and win things. I think he wants a higher base salary. That's our understanding.

But when the deadline eventually passed on Friday with no £120m bid from Man City, Chelsea sources said they expected Fernandez to stay until the end of the season. But that's no clear guarantee. They don't want the start of the season, the start of this new era dominated by conversations and questions for Xabi Alonso to answer every press conference. But one thing I will say, if Enzo Fernandez does stay he will be a massive part of Alonso's plans.

Who else could be on the way out before the deadline?

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sky Sports News' James Savundra with the latest on Chelsea's potential outgoings this summer transfer window

Will Chelsea play a back three?

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sky Sports News' David Richardson discusses how Chelsea could line-up under new boss Xabi Alonso

David Richardson: The big question around Xabi Alonso at Chelsea is whether he would replicate the 3-4-3 formation that he had such great success with at Bayer Leverkusen. Chelsea have played six pre-season games. In their first three, they played a back four, which was similar to what Alonso did at Real Madrid - and, as we know, it didn't go too well there. But since then, in the final three matches, he's played a back three and that has been when more of his senior players have been available to him.

In the first half against Real Sociedad, Chelsea sat too deep in the back three. It became almost a back five, with Marco Palestra and Pedro Neto as their wingbacks. They couldn't get out. They couldn't press. They became sloppy on the ball - and that was despite Morgan Rogers scoring after 10 minutes. They were much improved in the second half. They played higher up the pitch, dominated possession and because they were higher up the pitch, they were able to press.

Can Rogers and Palmer play together?

David Richardson: Rogers was on the left of the front three against Real Sociedad, with Joao Pedro through the middle and Palmer off the right. Rogers and Palmer didn't play as wingers; they were tucked in as inside forwards, which suits their game.

That is some front three. If you compare that to any other team in the league, it's got to be right up there - possibly the best front three in the division. Particularly with the way Joao Pedro is playing - he's scored seven goals in five games in pre-season. Rogers linked up well with Joao Pedro on Saturday, and it was probably him and Joao Pedro that showed more signs of connecting than Rogers and Palmer.

It's all about getting those front three firing. Palmer had that incredible first season at Chelsea and hasn't quite lived up to those standards. But having not been at the World Cup, he's had some rest, a full pre-season now and hopefully he'll be over those injuries that he's had in recent seasons and should be firing. It's a big, big season for him.

Who's the No 1?

David Richardson: It's a reflection on how well Robert Sanchez has started to do that he is still No 1. He had a much improved season last year. He played 51 times, a full season in goal and he looked more confident, more comfortable.

There were big question marks over his playing out from the back - I remember him being heckled by some Chelsea supporters to get the ball forward and just get it away from his own goal. But he's settled down now. Against Real Sociedad on Saturday, he made several saves in the first half, and he seems to be growing into that role.

As for Mike Penders, he came on as a substitute in that game but I think he'll have to wait for his opportunity. For now, it looks like Sanchez is Chelsea's No 1.

Why did Chelsea sign Henderson and Welbeck?

Image: Jordan Henderson signed a two-year deal with Chelsea

James Savundra: There have been so many silly yellow cards and that really did hamper Chelsea and a number of different managers couldn't solve it. Under Alonso and this new leadership group he's forming, when you consider the age of the players brought in, there's clearly been a lot of learning from the ownership group over the last four years.

Sometimes the approach was a bit scattergun when it came to transfers. But now I think Alonso has looked at the squad and realised 'we definitely need more experienced players that know how to win things'. That's players like Henderson and Welbeck, who can help these young players become players who can perform consistently in the Premier League and accept all that comes with being a Chelsea player.

These young players will need to deliver success - but now they've got real role models in the form of those more mature players. And actually even in the signings of Maxence Lacroix, who's 26, and Pep Chavarria, 28, I think it's clear that there's an admission that there have been mistakes made and everybody is seeing this as a new chapter.

What's success for Alonso and Chelsea this season?

James Savundra: It would be fascinating to be in those conversations and whether or not they've laid out clear defined targets for this season. I think they are really seeing this as a long-term project over two, three or four years and as long as they are seeing that progress on the pitch, whether or not they get Champions League football this season, I don't think that will define whether or not Xabi Alonso gets a second year.

It will be whether you can actually see with your eyes that this team is getting there, this culture is being built behind the scenes, because Alonso is going to be involved in a number of different areas at the club. But signing a player like Morgan Rogers for £117m? You're not spending this sort of money in the transfer window to finish in the top 10 or just to get Europa League football.

This season things have really opened up with a number of managerial changes. Liverpool a lot of upheaval there and that squad doesn't quite look ready for the start of the Premier League season. Manchester United, it's their first full season under Michael Carrick and how are they going to cope with playing in the Champions League as well?

So getting into the Champions League and having a really strong cup run in the FA Cup or the Carabao Cup will probably be the aim.

Sports.title: Rogers on playing with 'artist' Palmer and getting Chelsea back to the top
Sports.content:
Morgan Rogers is convinced Chelsea can once again compete for the top trophies and says he and Cole Palmer know exactly how to play together.

Rogers became the most expensive British player of all time when he joined Chelsea from Aston Villa straight after his World Cup exploits where he helped England reach the semi-finals and finish third in the tournament.

The 24-year-old scored on his debut in Chelsea's 3-1 win over Real Sociedad on Saturday.

"I'm just so excited," Rogers told Sky Sports. "It was just an unbelievable summer.

"It's probably the one summer where I didn't mind that it was a short one. I love my rest, I love my time with my family but at the same time it was one where I was watching the pre-season games, itching to just get back in.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Chelsea signed Rogers from Aston Villa in a record-breaking £117m deal

"I feel the excitement walking in every day. I feel the anticipation of not knowing where it can go. It can be good, it can be bad, but I feel a positive energy and a vibe. A fresh manager, a fresh change of environment, new players added and stuff - I feel that everyone's excited to see where it can go and where we can take it.

"Obviously, everyone's talking about it, who knows what we're going to do? But that's down to us and that's the thing - we've got a confident group of players that believe in ourselves and believe in each other's ability and our own.

Image: Rogers scored for Villa in last season's Europa League final and was also named player of the tournament

"Chelsea is a club that wants to win things. It's a club that I've always grown up watching win titles, win Champions Leagues and I want to be in teams that do that as well.

"The players - the Hazards, the Drogbas, the Lampards coming through when I was growing up watching football. It's a massive team and they were always winning and competing for titles and I want to be in teams that do that here.

"There's a lot of players in that room that have the aspirations to do the same thing, so it's exciting where we can take it.

"It's about knuckling down now and proving people wrong who probably had a negative outlook on Chelsea in the last couple of years. I'm excited, I'm positive and I can't wait really."

Rogers: Palmer and I will get the best out of each other

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Rogers talks about his friendship with Cole Palmer, whom he has known since the pair were teenagers

The move to Stamford Bridge reunites Rogers with former club team-mate Cole Palmer.

Rogers joined Manchester City as a teenager from West Brom and played with friend and fellow attacker Palmer for City at youth level as well as on England duty.

Rogers said: "I've seen people saying, 'how are you going to fit them in? How are they going to play?'

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player James Young from Genuis Sports compares the stats of new signing Rogers and Palmer at Chelsea

"We have completely different qualities. He's more of a passer, a linker, a combiner. He's like an artist in the way he moves with the ball and plays with it.

"I'm more direct, more straight line and more physical. We're completely different and that offsets really well.

"I've known his game, he's known my game since we were what, 14? We've played with each other at England and stuff like that, so we know exactly how to play with each other and to get the best out of each other.

Image: Rogers played regularly on the left wing and at No 10 for Aston Villa in the Premier League in 2025/26

"Some people might not know how it looks like, but we do. We know how it looks, we've done it before. People will pit us against each other, but we're on the same team now and it's about winning and getting the best out of each other, and I think we'll do that.

"Off the pitch always helps on the pitch - and playing with one of your closest friends always [helps] bring the best out of each other in a competitive way of wanting to kind of outdo each other. But there has to be a line of the team comes first, and winning comes first, and that's always been our biggest thing."

'I've got a lot more to come'

Image: Rogers' statistics while playing centrally or on the left last season

Rogers knows his price tag brings inevitable pressure, but trying to be the main man for club and country is something the forward says he relishes.

"This is what I live for. These are the conversations I want to be in," Rogers said.

"I want to be the topic of discussion when talking about games I'm involved in or England selections.

"I want to be in those conversations - sometimes on the good end of it, sometimes on the bad end of it - but if I'm in those conversations I'm doing something right.

"This summer I was getting into that and I was getting a taste for it of what it feels like. I know I've got a lot more to come and I like that pressure of it being on me where I've got the keys to decide how I'm spoken about in those conversations.

"If I've got the kind of say in what happens and what comes next then I'll be confident in myself to be on the right end of it."

Sports.title: Premier League to allow audio of conversations between players and referees
Sports.content:
The Premier League will permit audio of on-field conversations between players and referees during live broadcasts for the first time this season.

The use of audio by the Premier League’s domestic rights holders, Sky Sports and TNT Sports, is part of an expansion of the RefCam system, which became a permanent feature of top-flight coverage last season after a six-week trial at the start of the campaign. The head-mounted RefCams were used by broadcasters to provide near‑instant replays of match incidents from a new angle in an attempt to enhance the viewer experience, but under the terms of their agreement with clubs the audio captured by the cameras was not televised until several days later.

The Guardian has learned that the regulations will be relaxed this season, however, to permit a limited use of RefCam audio during live matches, with one or two incidents to be broadcast from each of the Premier League’s 38 match rounds. The audio will not be broadcast live or include any incidents that are referred to the video assistant referee, as that is not permitted under the laws of the game, which are set by the International Football Association Board (Ifab). The new audio offering will be made available as part of near-live instant replays, however, while the number of TV games featuring RefCam will increase from 20 to about 45.

Football has been slow to replicate the broadcasting innovations embraced by other sports, with in-match interviews and dressing rooms cameras long since accepted in cricket and both codes of rugby, as well as many American sports. Under increasing pressure from rights holders, football is belatedly looking to open up.

Sports.title: Enzo Maresca’s Manchester City opener was startlingly bad
Sports.content:
There are caveats. It was only the Community Shield – and no side has gone on to win the league after lifting the Community Shield since 2018. It was against the league champions, whose pre-season has involved far less strenuous travel than their own. By the time the season really gets going, there will be greater clarity in central midfield, with Rodri set to complete his move to Barcelona imminently. But this was a startlingly bad opening for Enzo Maresca at Manchester City.

Succeeding a manager of Pep Guardiola’s stature is never easy, as numerous clubs have found. But it’s not just Guardiola’s stature, the sense that whoever follows him stands in his shadow. It’s that his style of play is so idiosyncratic that the transition process inevitably becomes more difficult. Even though Maresca was Guardiola’s assistant at City in 2022-23, and his football is Guardiola-inspired, it is not identical, not least because Guardiola was always evolving. Even allowing for all that, though, it was remarkable how poorly City defended in their 3-0 defeat by Arsenal on Sunday.

Arsenal played well. There was a sharpness to them and a slickness to their passing that wasn’t always present last season. Fears that they may have lost their appetite having ended their 22-year wait for the title may have been overstated (although much, much tougher tests await). But City were a rabble, limited going forward and a shambles at the back.

It was the second goal that will really have worried them, because Arsenal had to do so little to score. Martin Ødegaard was given time to measure his cross. Christos Tzolis wandered off the back of Abdukodir Khusanov. Then Kai Havertz, slightly more explicably, pulled away from Rúben Dias. In Khusanov’s defence, it probably should be acknowledged that he does not usually play at right-back, but he has occupied the role before. A wide player drifting off your back should not come as a shock; perhaps it’s just pre-season and he was not as alert as he will be, but it was a baffling error. But it was of a piece with the wider whole; throughout, City seemed off the pace, not as focused as Arsenal. Even if that improves as the season goes on, it’s a problem if City have title aspirations; how far clear will Arsenal be by the time City finally click – if they do click?

But there were structural issues on that flank as well. Antoine Semenyo was barely involved. Elliot Anderson, on the right of the midfield two, was unable to check the forward surges of Riccardo Calafiori, who scored the first and whose run played a key role in the third. An attacking left-back, even one with as much freedom to drift infield as the Italian enjoys, shouldn’t cause that much trouble.

The midfield issue desperately needs resolving. Rodri was an unused substitute as talks about his possible likely move to Barcelona go on (City accepted a bid for him on Sunday night). It’s not just his quality that will be missed; his organisational abilities will be too. Enzo Fernández, who worked with Maresca at Chelsea, did seem to have been lined up as a replacement for Rodri but City did not submit a bid before the Friday 5pm deadline Chelsea had placed for selling the midfielder. Mateo Kovacic spent much of last season deputising for Rodri but he is 32 now; he is not the future. Factor in the loss of Bernardo Silva as well, and there is a serious shortfall in midfield.

Generally, in fact, City’s squad looks a little short. Dias and Marc Guéhi are the only defenders over 25. There are plenty of attacking midfielders but Omar Marmoush has never really convinced as a back-up to Erling Haaland. The £200m spree in January 2025 may have helped stop the rot, but the players who came in then – not just Marmoush and Khusanov but also Vitor Reis and Nico González – would not be badly missed now. City, once so focused in their spending, have started to make mistakes. Tijjani Reijnders, brought in last summer for £50m, is about to be shipped on. Rayan Aït-Nouri was a baffling signing when he arrived and nothing in the past year has changed that view.

Maresca must have looked at Arsenal’s squad, the extraordinary options available to Mikel Arteta in midfield, and despaired. Put generously, his is a squad in transition, although it’s starting to look as though it may be a squad in decline. The sense over the past couple of years was of Guardiola, slowly, passing his peak, but in retrospect perhaps it was only his genius that kept an ailing City competitive.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Twice weekly Sign up to Soccer Desk Jonathan Wilson and Guardian journalists bring expert analysis and reporting on the biggest stories in soccer. Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

The evidence of Sunday, with all due caveats about the stage of the season, is that this may be a very bad time for Maresca to have replaced Guardiola. Taking over from a legend would be extremely challenging in the best of circumstances, and these are starting to look like they may be very bad circumstances.

Sports.title: Premier League 2026-27 preview No 12: Ipswich
Sports.content:
Guardian writers’ predicted position: 19th (NB: this is not necessarily Will Unwin’s prediction but the average of our writers’ tips)

Last season’s position: 2nd (Championship)

Prospects

Back for another crack at the Premier League, the Tractor Boys are taking things very seriously. More than £100m has been spent on 10 new arrivals in an attempt to make the team fit for purpose, something that could not be said two years ago when they were relegated without being competitive after focusing on signing the Championship’s finest. Being the league’s fourth-biggest net spenders has created quiet optimism in Suffolk that things will go better this time. Lessons were learned, even if their galling relegation benefited the careers of Liam Delap and Omari Hutchinson, as the harsh reality of what happens when potential meets proven quality.

Ensuring there is a core of players with Premier League experience has been fundamental. Issa Diop and Sasa Lukic joined from Fulham, while Florentino Luís was snapped up after his baptism at Burnley to give a strong spine. The search for new players has stretched further and wider than in recent seasons, too, in a bid to find better valued talent than is available in England. Luís and Lukic are required to provide physicality and a desire to win the ball back in the centre of the park, although another addition in there would be advantageous.

The new manager, Gary O’Neil, has the right battling qualities and intelligence to keep a side up, explaining why he was the man quickly targeted to replace the outgoing Kieran McKenna, who resigned after securing promotion. The constant cheque-signing may explain the slow start to pre-season, losing to Osasuna, as everyone learned about O’Neil’s methods and demands, but they looked effective against Rayo Vallecano and the return of Julio Enciso will add some much-needed creativity and ingenuity.

If all else fails, Ipswich will at least make history after signing goalkeeper Kjell Scherpen, who at 6ft9 is set to become the Premier League’s tallest ever player.

Off-field picture

Work on a £30m training ground upgrade is close to completion. The regeneration will include a new first-team building, in addition to improved facilities for the academy and women’s team. The construction was seen as necessary to bring the club in line with their rivals and help convince potential signings Suffolk is the place to be. In a rarity, the club’s main shirt sponsor is a local business, the software company Halo. Ed Sheeran, meanwhile, is still represented on the kit with his ‘Play’ featuring on the sleeves.

Owner-fan relationship

Being successful is always good for morale, and members of the Gamechanger 20 ownership group could be found celebrating promotion with fans in the town centre. They have made a number of promises since taking over the club in 2021 and have delivered on them all. The one blot was the decision to invite the Reform UK leader, Nigel Farage, to Portman Road, which was a PR disaster, creating a needless – and embarrassing – circus around the club, as Ipswich struggled to create a cohesive story about the situation, which was only forgotten thanks to them reaching the Premier League.

The manager

It was a surprise when the universally popular McKenna decided to leave after securing another promotion, forcing some quick thinking to find a replacement. O’Neil has plenty of experience from his time managing Bournemouth and Wolves, added to with a spell at Strasbourg, but has a tough act to follow. Always open and honest, his coaching career has been spent trying to keep teams above the red line. His time at Wolves ended poorly but circumstances dictated much of that as the club failed to invest, something he can’t say in his new role.

Star signing

View image in fullscreen Emersonn comes in in the for decent money from French side Toulouse, can he keep Ipswich in the division? Photograph: Keeran Marquis/NurPhoto/Shutterstock

Emersonn is the record signing, costing £24m from Toulouse, and he has the difficult task of providing the goals that could bring safety, although he is yet to prove himself as a consistent scorer. The 22-year-old is the first Brazilian to play for the Tractor Boys but had to work hard in pre-season to catch up with his colleagues, having arrived lacking the necessary fitness levels. Eager to run in behind, he will be dangerous against teams who leave space. He has all the attributes to excel but it is down to him and the coaches aligning to ensure that this expensive gamble pays off.

Stat attack

Last season, Ipswich were masters of exploiting high turnovers. They generated shots from 22.2% of them, more than double the Championship’s average rate of 10.4%. If O’Neil can maintain this efficiency, it could be Ipswich’s most effective method of creating chances.

Set for a breakthrough

The £17.5m fee for a then 19-year-old showed what Ipswich thought of Sindre Walle Egeli, the son of a former Norwegian lower league footballer. The record goalscorer for Norway at youth level has naturally drawn comparisons to a certain Erling Haaland, who has given advice to his compatriot and may have the chance to offer more in person when Ipswich come up against Manchester City. A boyhood Liverpool fan, his first year in England brought four Championships goals in 18 starts, laying the groundwork as he and his teammates look to step up. Walle Egeli returned after the break in fine shape and has looked promising in the No 10 position under O’Neil, having previously played out wide.

World Cup impact

After suffering a rather pathetic relegation to League One with Leicester, Abdul Fatawu joined up with the Ghana squad for the World Cup. He came on in each of his country’s four matches but playing as a winger for Carlos Queiroz was not particularly fun. The Black Stars were ultra-defensive, scoring only twice as they limped out of the tournament as one of the most forgettable teams involved. Fatawu will be hoping for more creative freedom under O’Neil as he desperately seeks to avoid a third straight relegation.

Sports.title: Rodri set to complete Barcelona move after Manchester City accept £65.4m bid
Sports.content:
Rodri looks set to complete a move to Barcelona after Manchester City accepted a bid of £65.4m from the Spanish club.

The 30-year-old World Cup winner had entered the final year of his contract at the Etihad Stadium and made it clear he would like the opportunity to move to Barcelona. City, who are now closing in on a deal to sign Lille’s Ayyoub Bouaddi, were reluctant sellers but had little choice with the Spanish international out of contract next summer.

City had already rejected Barcelona’s bid of around €60m (£51m) for Rodri last week after an initial offer of €45m (£38.5m) but have now accepted the latest bid.

Speaking after City’s 3-0 Community Shield defeat by Arsenal on Sunday, Enzo Maresca called Rodri a “top player” and said “all the teams need Rodri”, but City have been unable to persuade their linchpin to stay and sign a new contract. Rodri had only returned to the club on Friday, having undergone back surgery after the World Cup, with Maresca saying he had given him a “big hug” when he first met up with him.

Rodri has spent seven seasons with City, winning the Premier League four times and scoring the only goal when they beat Inter in the 2023 Champions League final. The following year he won the Ballon d’Or but, by the time he was presented with the trophy, he was sidelined with an anterior cruciate ligament which ruled him out of most of the 2024-25 campaign, while hamstring and groin problems limited him to 33 appearances in Pep Guardiola’s final campaign in charge.

City have already undergone major changes in midfield this summer, spending £116m on Elliot Anderson, while agreeing a deal to sell Tijjani Reijnders to Al Qadsiah. They are now ready to seal a move for the Morocco star Bouaddi.

The teenager impressed at the World Cup and Lille had initially wanted any potential move to include a 12-month loan deal back to the French side. However, with City losing Bernardo Silva and now Rodri, Maresca is keen to bulk up his midfield options for the new campaign and want Bouaddi available for this season. City have also been linked with Chelsea’s Enzo Fernández and retain an interest.

Sports.title: Brighton’s Emilie Joramo: ‘I feel like I’m now in the place I want to be’
Sports.content:
Emilie Joramo has long had her sights set on the Women’s Super League, but she held herself back from pushing for a move over from Scandinavia – until now.

“I’d been interested in the league for a long time now and it was a goal for me to get here one day,” says Joramo, who Brighton signed on a free transfer at the end of June. “It was about finding the right path for me to get here. I didn’t want to go too early, I wanted to feel ready for it both physically and mentally. Now, everything just felt right.”

Brighton had been tracking the Norwegian midfielder for some time and the 24-year-old was aware of their interest. An encouraging conversation with Brighton’s manager, Dario Vidosic, and good meetings with the club as her contract with Hammarby drew closer to its end meant she was at last ready to join the league she had followed from afar.

That time in Sweden with Hammarby, with whom she reached the Europa Cup final last season, and before that in her homeland with Rosenborg who she helped win the Norwegian Cup for the first time in 21 years, was crucial in preparing her for her latest challenge.

“I had so much fun at Hammarby and I’ve got so many good friends there,” she says. “I grew both as a football player and as a person in those years. I didn’t feel ready when I was 21, when I went to Sweden, to come over here. I felt like I needed to play a bit more, to play every game, that was really important for me.”

That Brighton had been aware of her for some time was a boost too. “It’s reassuring for me that they really wanted me,” she says. “They hadn’t just watched a couple games, they’d been following me for years, and that’s really important to me because I’m not going to jump at the first opportunity I get. I like to think things through and it has to feel right for me.”

View image in fullscreen Emilie Joramo played Champions League qualifying last year, and helped Hammarby reach the final of the inaugural Europa Cup Photograph: Emma Wallskog/Bildbyrån/Shutterstock

For Brighton fans wondering what they are getting, there should be some excitement too. Joramo is fiercely motivated and feels she fits the possession-based style of football that Vidosic wants his team to play.

“I would say that I’m a hardworking player,” she says, when asked to describe herself. “I always give 100% all of the time. I can’t do 50, 60, 70, I’m always 100%. I want to have the ball. I want to play, not just put balls in behind but to keep the ball , play with each other, [build] good relationships with the other players and think several steps ahead. They’ve always been things that I’m good at and I’m always wanting to get better at too.”

Brighton and the WSL present a step up. “I think I can get challenged a lot here because things go much faster, the intensity is higher, you have a smaller amount of time when you have the ball,” she says. “So, it’s a perfect place for me to be at now to be challenged further and develop my strengths but also the parts that I’m not as strong at and need to develop more.”

Arriving and starting life on the south coast was “a bit overwhelming” in the beginning: “There’s so many people to get to know, the staff is so much bigger than what I’ve been used to. So, instead of one physio you have five and you need to get to know everyone and get to know which person does which role. That’s always the way it is in a new team, of course, but it’s much bigger here.”

Everyone has been very welcoming and her first impressions of training sessions under Vidosic have been positive. “I’ve only had two sessions with him so far,” she says, “but he seems very, very good at football tactics, how the game works, how to play good football, and that was important for me because I’m a player that wants to have the ball and always wants to try to get better and try to play good football together as a team, not only as individuals. This is what Dario wants, so it really fits my ambitions, my values and how I want to play.”

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Weekly Sign up to Moving the Goalposts No topic is too small or too big for us to cover as we deliver a twice-weekly roundup of the wonderful world of women’s football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

View image in fullscreen Emilie Joramo was Brighton’s second signing of the summer window – they have since added five more. Photograph: James Boardman/Brighton and Hove Albion

She is finding her feet on the pitch, and starting to find them off it. Joramo’s girlfriend has moved to England with her, which has helped the transition and helps her escape football when needed. “I have to have other things to do besides football,” she says. “We’ve been to the beach and have been exploring the city. It’s so different for me to live by the beach, I’m from the mountains and the woods. This is like a holiday for me, and with the weather as well, it’s been so warm. It’s really nice.”

The goal now is “to contribute as much as I can to this team and play as much as I can”, but Joramo’s patience as she worked towards her WSL goal should continue to serve her well. “I feel like I’m now in the place I want to be and develop in and I need to give it a bit of time in the beginning, because I can be very impatient,” she says. “I have to give it some time to get into it, get into the intensity and everything around the game here, because it’s so much more than what I’m used to in Sweden, this is so much bigger.”

At the end of her first season in England is a big carrot, should Norway come through a two-legged playoff against Romania and then another against Albania or Wales and qualify for the 2027 Women’s World Cup.

Joramo made her debut for the senior side in 2022 and has been on the fringes of the squad since, making three appearances in total and playing for the under-23s. In April she was on the bench for the senior side’s back-to-back qualification campaign wins over Slovenia and she is hopeful her WSL move helps her show what she can bring.

“Hopefully this also will strengthen my opportunities with the national team,” she says. “I know this is the best league in the world, so if I get to play here, then I’ve done something right, I think.”

Sports.title: Baller League to no longer be shown live on Sky Sports from next season
Sports.content:
Sky Sports will not broadcast next season’s Baller League, the celebrity six-a-side competition backed by the influencer KSI, the actor Idris Elba and former players including Ian Wright and Alan Shearer.

KSI’s Prime FC won last season’s Baller League final at a sold-out O 2 Arena in an event broadcast live on Sky. But the Guardian has learned the broadcaster has opted not to renew the contract next season. While Sky was happy with audience numbers, and particularly the level of engagement on social media, sources say the partnership had come to a natural end.

Baller League was launched in Germany in 2024 with backing from the World Cup winners Mats Hummels and Lukas Podolski before expanding rapidly. A UK edition took place for the first time in 2025, with the former players Jens Lehmann and Micah Richards and the England Lioness Chloe Kelly all taking on management roles with one of the 12 teams. A US tournament was held for the first time this year.

The creation of Baller League continues a trend of short-form celebrity tournaments which was started by the former Spain international Gerard Piqué, who in 2022 set up the seven-a-side Kings League, which now takes place in eight countries and has a broadcast deal with Dazn.

Felix Starck, chief executive of the Baller League, told the Guardian that it had not sought an extension with Sky as it wants to make its events available free-to-air. As a result, Baller League will focus on its existing distribution with YouTube next season, although it is understood that discussions did take place with Sky’s parent company, Comcast, over a wider investment partnership that will not proceed.

Sports.title: ‘I’ll remember it for the rest of my life’: the footballers whose biggest games come before their league begins
Sports.content:
Premier League footballers are gearing up for the start of the season, but some of their fellow professionals in smaller leagues across Europe have been going all summer – even those who play a winter campaign. Some played the biggest games of their lives when the rest of us were watching the World Cup. The Champions League qualifiers began when the World Cup was at the last-16 stage, with some clubs already knocked out of Europe by the time England were beaten by Argentina in Atlanta.

Larne, the champions of Northern Ireland, began their European crusade on the day Argentina beat Egypt in the World Cup last-16, Dan Bent’s penalty in the second leg a week later helping them overcome Tre Fiori of San Marino in the Champions League. Larne’s reward was a meeting with former European champions Red Star Belgrade. They were beaten 9-0 on aggregate by the Serbian giants, but it is an experience Bent will treasure for ever.

“Red Star was probably the biggest game in the club’s history,” says the centre-back. “When the draw came out, we were ecstatic. You want to play those games in those stadiums. Everyone tells you about how long the tunnel is and how intimidating it is, and then you’re there and a part of it. There were 27,000 fans and the funny thing is, for them, that’s a medium-sized crowd. The stadium was only half-full.” The population of Larne could have fit into the rest of it with room to spare.

View image in fullscreen Dan Bent playing for Larne at Red Star Belgrade in the Champions League qualifiers. Photograph: Anadolu/Getty Images

“Red Star were just another level,” he says. “You don’t realise until you’re in amongst it. You do your best, but sometimes there are gaps that are hard to bridge. But to play in that competition, at that ground, against a team as big as that, was amazing. I’ll remember it for the rest of my life.”

The European qualifiers move fast, with teams given little time to prepare or analyse opponents. “It’s a privilege to play in Champions League qualifiers but a lot of uncertainty comes with that,” says Bent. “In early June you know your first Champions League game would be around the first week of July, so you can gear up for that. But after that, each week will just change depending on results.

“One minute, we could be heading to Rangers or Slovakia, the next we’re going to Gibraltar or Cyprus. You might be playing one team who could play in a totally different way to the other, or we might want to play in a different way against them. You need to pick up things quickly. It’s a quick turnaround. Logistically, it is pretty crazy. You have to plan for all eventualities.”

If players find it unnerving, imagine the stress for the clubs’ operations managers and the players’ families. “I’ve got a partner and two children and it is hard for them,” says Bent. “She’s very supportive and understands, but it doesn’t get any easier knowing I’m away for three days, then the week after I could be flying out again to another country. It helps when you have a good family around you who understand the demands of football. They know it’s a positive thing because not many people are able to play in Champions League qualifiers.”

Bent is used to living out of a suitcase and jumping on a plane every few days. He grew up in Kent and started his career at Gillingham. After being released in 2015 when he was a teenager, he took a scholarship in America. He played college and semi-professional soccer in Georgia, Ohio and South Carolina before moving to Gibraltar to play for Magpies, Manchester 62 and then Lincoln Red Imps – who are Larne’s next European opponents.

After losing to Red Star in the Champions League, Larne dropped into the Europa League qualifiers where they were narrowly beaten in extra time by Georgian club Iberia 1999. Now they face the Gibraltan champions over two legs for a place in the Conference League group stage, the first leg on Thursday seeing an emotional return for Bent, who spent long enough in Gibraltar to become eligible for the national team and earn 17 caps.

View image in fullscreen Dan Bent celebrates after converting a penalty against Tre Fiori in the Champions League first qualifying round in July. Photograph: Inpho/Shutterstock

The tie is a huge opportunity for both clubs. Larne beat the Red Imps at this stage two years ago and booked their place in the Conference League group stage, securing €2.6m in prize money. Considering that clubs are awarded around £50,000 for winning the league in Northern Ireland and just £20,000 for winning the cup, that is transformational money for the club and players – who earn hefty bonuses for European victories.

“There’s a big core of boys who were here when they got to the group phase, so they talk about that,” says Bent. “They played games all the way up until Christmas. They’ve been there and they want to go back.” The group stage is also a prominent shop window. It’s not just Bodø/Glimt players who are earning transfers off the back of repeated impressive performances in European competitions.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Being able to drop through Uefa’s three tiers can be a gamechanger for players’ careers. “That’s where the hard work of winning the league previously comes to fruition,” says Bent. “You go through the whole year to win the league, to make sure you’ll have a summer of European football. If you go out of the Champions League, you’re going to be dropping down and having a few games. I do enjoy that.”

These second and third chances mean a lot of players are racking up considerable European records. “I’m probably up there in terms of European experience,” says Bent, who will play in Europe for the 21st time when Larne visit Gibraltar on Thursday night. “Our goalkeeper, Rohan Ferguson, has something like 40 appearances in Europe. We have boys who’ve been great servants in the league but haven’t played a lot of European football, and young lads with that fresh hunger, wanting to play in it. It’s a well-balanced group.”

Larne kicked off their title defence with a hard-fought goalless draw at Coleraine over the weekend and the second leg of their tie against Lincoln Red Imps next week will be their 10th match in five competitions this season. But you won’t hear them complaining. They are having life-enriching experiences on their European expeditions.

This is an article by Gavin Willacy for Playing in the Shadows

Sports.title: Tottenham goalkeeper Guglielmo Vicario to leave for Juventus in loan deal
Sports.content:
Juventus have agreed a deal with Tottenham for Guglielmo Vicario to join on an initial loan after the Italian side decided against a move for Aston Villa’s Emiliano Martínez.

Vicario is set to leave Spurs having lost his place as Roberto De Zerbi’s No 1 to Antonin Kinsky, with the agreement with Juventus containing an option to make the Italy goalkeeper’s move permanent next year for £8.6m. Martínez had been linked with the Turin club after Villa agreed a deal to sign Parma’s Zion Suzuki for around £30m but Juventus saw a €10m offer rejected over the weekend and decided to switch their attention elsewhere. The Argentina goalkeeper is currently sidelined due to a finger injury.

Vicario moved to north London in 2023 for £17.2m and has made almost 120 appearances since then. With De Zerbi having also brought in Martin Dubravka on a free transfer as cover for Kinsky, the 29-year-old will become the latest player to leave Spurs this summer after Cristian Romero, Djed Spence, Will Lankshear and Yves Bissouma. Pape Matar Sarr is also wanted by Everton and Nottingham Forest. The Senegal midfielder is valued at £30m.

Spurs have already spent more than £200m on six new players in this transfer window and are keen on signing Savinho from Manchester City. The Brazil forward was not part of Enzo Maresca’s squad for the Community Shield defeat to Arsenal in Cardiff and is thought to be open to the move. Spurs have also been heavily linked with a move for Liverpool’s Cody Gakpo as De Zerbi seeks to strengthen his attack.

Coventry have signed the striker Taiwo Awoniyi from Nottingham Forest for £9m.

The 29-year-old scored 23 times in 103 appearances across all competitions for Forest after joining in 2022. But the Nigeria international was limited to just three starts in the league last season and will be looking for more game time at the Coventry Building Society Arena.

“I am very excited about this season, and I can’t wait to get started,” he said.

“I’m really looking forward to working with my new teammates. I have seen how amazing they have been last season, coming up from the Championship. They were incredible.”

Ipswich have raided Gary O’Neil’s old club Strasbourg for Abdoul Ouattara and Julio Enciso before Saturday’s Premier League opener at home to Sunderland.

Ex-Brighton attacker Enciso enjoyed a productive six-month loan at Portman Road during the club’s last season in the top flight and has signed a five-year deal with the Suffolk club. “I really enjoyed my time on loan at the club and I was so happy to see them win promotion back to the Premier League last season,” Enciso told the official club website.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

“I worked with the manager in France last season and the chance to play for him again at a great club like Ipswich is one I’m very excited for.”

Côte d’Ivoire youngster Ouattara has also linked up with his old coach O’Neil at Ipswich and put pen to paper on a contract until 2031.

Sports.title: Former ball boy to land huge windfall as Au Vodka brand ‘strikes £500m sale agreement’
Sports.content:
Former ball boy to land huge windfall as Au Vodka brand ‘strikes £500m sale agreement’

A former foe of Eden Hazard is set to give his bank balance an almighty boost.

Charlie Morgan, the infamous ball boy Hazard kicked during a League Cup match in 2013 between Swansea City and Chelsea, is nearing a deal to sell his drinks company, Au Vodka.



2 Hazard received a red card for kicking Morgan Credit: Getty

Morgan is in discussions to sell Au Vodka to American beverage brand Sazerac Company.

How much does Charlie Morgan stand to make from Au Vodka sale?

The sale of Au Vodka is worth approximately £500million, with Morgan and co-founder Jackson Quinn to net £100m each from the deal.

Sazerac owns alcoholic brands like BuzzBallz, Southern Comfort and Fireball.



And Au Vodka, founded by Morgan in 2015, now looks poised to join them under the Sazerac umbrella.

Au Vodka's impending sale comes a year after Morgan told BBC Wales he intended to expand his drinks brand into the American market.



"If you asked a 25-year-old target market consumer in America, would they know Au? Probably not yet," Morgan said.

"So there's still so many more people who don't know about us.

"And I think we're still driven to try and take over the world a little bit more."



Who has endorsed Au Vodka in the past?

Au Vodka is widely known for its gold-coloured bottles and cans, with several celebrities endorsing the beverage.

Football legend Ronaldinho and boxing superstar Floyd Mayweather have both happily posed alongside Au Vodka products.

2 Mayweather had little hesitation in showing himself off with some Au Vodka bottles Credit: Instagram/@AuVodka

YouTuber-turned-boxer Jake Paul even went as far as getting a tattoo of an Au Vodka bottle, although there was plenty of conjecture as to whether it was a real piece of body art.



Meanwhile, two-time darts world champion Luke Littler was another who has been a beneficiary of Au Vodka's generosity.

Upon turning 18 in January 2025, Littler was gifted a three-little Au Vodka bottle.

On the bottle was an image of Littler lifting the Sid Waddell Trophy shortly after his maiden World Darts Championship triumph.

That wasn't the only show-stopping gift headed Littler's way from Morgan's company.



Littler also received a giant gold dart which featured his nickname, 'The Nuke', on the flight.

Sports.title: Premier League club told to re-hire Steve Bruce as sack prediction made
Sports.content:
Hull City manager Sergej Jakirovic has been tipped to be the first Premier League boss to be sacked this season.

And as a replacement, the Tigers will have a few options: Kieran McKenna, Scott Parker and even Steve Bruce.



3 Jakirovic has been tipped to be the first manager sacked in the Premier League this season Credit: Getty

Hull achieved promotion back to the Premier League for the first time since 2017 last term by winning the Championship Play-Off Final against Middlesbrough at Wembley.

Jakirovic was tasked with keeping the club in the second tier, but he incredibly ended up leading them to the top flight.

They are heavily predicted to be relegated this season though, and if they do struggle as expected, the Serbian could be sacked.



At least that's what former Premier League striker Troy Deeney thinks, as he tipped Jakirovic to be an early departure.

"I feel the Hull manager may go," Deeney stated on talkSPORT's Premier League All Access podcast when predicting which manager will be sacked first this campaign.



"If in the first month they're not doing well and the window's closed, he's the only one that can get changed, right?"

Who could potentially replace Jakirovic?

Should Deeney's prediction of Jakirovic's sacking come true, Hull will then have to bring a new boss into the dugout.



And host Sam Matterface began: "There are a few managers doing the rounds that could step into the breach..."

He went on to mention McKenna, who left Ipswich earlier this summer, and former Burnley boss Parker.

But Alex Crook bravely asked: "Get Steve Bruce back there?"

3 Bruce (right) spent four years as Hull manager from 2012, achieving two promotions Credit: Getty

Bruce was Hull manager for four years from 2012 through to 2016, taking charge of 201 games across his tenure.



He won 85 of those matches, winning promotion to the Premier League twice and leading the Tigers to the FA Cup final in 2014, which in turn secured a spot in a European competition for the first time in the club's history the following season.

The 65-year-old, who is a regular on talkSPORT, hasn't had a job since October 2025, when he was sacked by Blackpool.

What other Premier League managers are at risk of an early sacking?

Jakirovic wasn't the only sacking prediction made on the Premier League All Access podcast, as another name popped up.

New Fulham manager Alvaro Arbeloa is also at risk of being the first let go by their club this year, according to Matterface and Crook.



Matterface explained: "He's a rookie manager, he's following a man who built something that absolutely worked.

3 Arbeloa has also been mentioned as a potential first sacking of the season Credit: Getty

"They've sold their goals, there's no goals in that team. I just can't see it working out for him."

Pierre Sage was also mentioned by Deeney as another potential manager who could face an early sacking this season.



Sage recently took over from Oliver Glasner at Crystal Palace.

The 2026/27 Premier League campaign gets started on Friday, with champions Arsenal facing Coventry, live on talkSPORT.

Commentary from the Emirates will be coming from Jim Proudfoot and former Palace manager Alan Pardew.
