Sports.title: Harry Kane and Kylian Mbappe tipped to be beaten to Ballon d’Or by Champions League winner
Sports.content:
Harry Kane and Kylian Mbappe tipped to be beaten to Ballon d’Or by Champions League winner

Khvicha Kvaratskhelia has been tipped to be this year's surprise Ballon d'Or winner, ahead of Harry Kane and Kylian Mbappe.

Kane and Mbappe are among the frontrunners to claim football's biggest individual prize after the pair enjoyed stunning years for both club and country respectively.



5 Kvaratskhelia is arguably the best winger in world football right now Credit: Getty

After a record-breaking 61-goal campaign for Bayern Munich, Kane backed up his claim for the prestigious award by firing in six goals for England at this summer's World Cup.

But he faces stiff competition here, with France megastar Mbappe joined in the running by World Cup winner Lamine Yamal.

With the competition having a major bearing on the Ballon d'Or in recent years, Kane's England teammate Jude Bellingham and football icon Lionel Messi have also entered the fold off the back of standout summers, battling it out for the Golden Boot.



Kvaradona for the win?

With World Cup stars dominating the Ballon d'Or conversation, European football expert Andy Brassell has instead pointed to a player who played no part in North America this summer.

He called Paris Saint-Germain forward Kvaratskhelia a real contender for the award, pointing to his stunning campaign at club level.



The Georgian played a major role as PSG clinched back-to-back Champions League crowns in May, by beating Arsenal in the final.

Kvaratskhelia registered 17 goal contributions in 16 European games last term, which saw him named the 2025/26 Champions League Player of the Season for the first time in his career.



And Brassell believes his stunning performances in club football's biggest competition place him among the world's very best.

Discussing Kvaratskhelia on the Trans Euro Express, Brassell said: "If not the best in the world, really close

"I think to have that amount of ability on the ball, to bring it to bear usefully for the team and to do as much as he does without the ball, what more could you want from a football player?

5 Kane is a contender for the Ballon d'Or after a stunning season for club and country Credit: Getty



5 Kvaratskhelia showcased all of his world class ability in PSG's recent Super Cup win Credit: Getty

"He's got it all, and he's still only 25."

Brassell then tipped Kvaratskhelia as a major Ballon d'Or candidate, insisting his chances have been boosted after other favourites failed to take their chance this summer.

Victory in either of club or international football's biggest tournaments can be decisive in securing the individual award.

But with the likes of Kane, Mbappe, Messi and Bellingham missing out on World Cup glory, Brassell believes the conversation then moves back to the Champions League, where Kvaratskhelia reigned supreme.



He continued: "In terms of the Ballon d'Or, there's a chance because none of the players who could have made it theirs did.

"If Argentina win the World Cup final, Messi wins it. If England win it, then either (Harry) Kane or maybe (Jude) Bellingham win it.

5 Mbappe clinched the 2026 World Cup Golden Boot by firing in ten goals Credit: Getty

“If France win it, then Mbappe's got a case, and maybe a little side chance of Michael Olise. But none of those things came to pass.



"So eyes go back to the Champions League, and who was the best player in the Champions League last season?"

'He's been the standout player'

Brassell isn't alone in tipping Kvaratskhelia to win the Ballon d'Or - talkSPORT's Gabby Agbonlahor made a similar case in July.

The former Aston Villa hero insisted the 25-year-old has had a bigger impact than other contenders, insisting World Cup winner Yamal and Kane were less decisive for their respective teams.

Agbonlahor told talkSPORT: "Do you know the player that I would give it to? [Kvicha] Kvaratskhelia.



"But if you think about the best player to watch with your two eyes has been Kvaratskhelia all season for PSG.

5 Khvicha Kvaratskhelia scored 19 goals in all competitions for PSG in the 2025/26 campaign Credit: Getty

"He's been the standout player – more than Lamine Yamal; more than Harry Kane; more than everyone else."

Sports.title: Manchester United to instantly reject European club’s audacious bid for Bruno Fernandes
Sports.content:
Manchester United consider Bruno Fernandes not for sale at any price, talkSPORT understands.

The Red Devils will immediately reject any offers for their superstar captain amid interest from Galatasaray.

3 Man United consider Fernandes not for sale at any price this summer Credit: Getty

The Turkish giants are prepared to make a £42.7million bid, but they are yet to send their approach to United.

And if they do, the Red Devils have no intention of accepting it.

Galatasaray are understood to be open to offering Fernandes a lucrative four-year contract at the club to try and tempt him.

However, the Portugal international has not indicated to Man United that he wants to leave to date.

The club don't want him to leave either, with United not looking to engage with any other teams over a sale.

Fernandes did have a £57m release clause in his contract, but that has now expired.

His current deal at Old Trafford expires next summer.

Man United's change of stance

The 13-time Premier League winners will not be selling their skipper this summer amid exit links, which also arose last year.

In 2025, Fernandes turned down a massive £700,000-a-week contract with Saudi club Al Hilal to stay in Manchester.

He made that decision despite feeling that Man United wanted him to depart, which was something he revealed in December.

3 Fernandes' future at Old Trafford was also a debate last year Credit: Getty

"I could have left like many people do and said, 'I want to leave, I don’t want to train, I just want to leave for €20million or €30million , so they pay me more on the other side'," Fernandes admitted.

"But I never did that. I never felt in a position to do that, because I felt that the empathy and affection I had for the club were the same.

"But there comes a point where, for them, money is more important than anything. The club wanted me to go, I have that in my head.

"I told the directors this, but I think they didn’t have the courage to make that decision...from the club’s side, I felt a bit like, 'If you leave, it’s not so bad for us.'

"It hurts me a lot. More than hurting, it makes me sad because I’m a player they have nothing to criticise about."

Now, a year later, Man United are set on keeping Fernandes as they head into the new Premier League season.

3 Fernandes is going to stay at the club and lead them into another season Credit: Getty

Michael Carrick's side take on newly-promoted Hull City in their opening game of the campaign on Saturday.

Sports.title: Taiwo Awoniyi leaves Nottingham Forest for Premier League rivals as deal confirmed
Sports.content:
Nottingham Forest striker Taiwo Awoniyi has completed his move to Coventry City.

Awoniyi, who signed for Forest in 2022, has completed a medical and joined Coventry in a £9million deal.



3 Awoniyi has played over 100 games for Forest but he's set to leave for Coventry Credit: Getty

The Nigeria international is delighted to have made the move, telling the club's website: “I’m very happy to complete my move to Coventry City.

“I am very excited about this season, and I can’t wait to get started.

“I’m really looking forward to working with my new teammates, I have seen how amazing they have been last season, coming up from the Championship, they were incredible and now I am just excited to join them and get started for the new season.”



Coventry manager Frank Lampard is said to have had a big say in signing the forward, pushing to get a move over the line.

Awoniyi featured regularly for Forest during pre-season, scoring one goal under new boss Oliver Glasner in recent weeks.



But a 45-minute appearance against Bayer Leverkusen proved to be his final appearance for the club.

Awoniyi on the move

Awoniyi was not guaranteed to be playing first-team football under Glasner this season, due to his many attacking options.



Chris Wood, Igor Jesus, Dan Ndoye and Arnaud Kalimuendo are all players who can lead the line for Forest.

So, the 29-year-old forward is making a move to their Midlands rivals, joining up with Lampard and Coventry.

Awoniyi will depart Forest after making 103 appearances for the club, scoring 23 goals and providing six assists altogether.

Last season, he played 17 Premier League games but started just three, scoring four goals and setting up one.



He was also left out of their Europa League squad, sitting out of all of their games played on the continent.

Coventry's summer business so far

Championship winners Coventry have already made six summer signings, breaking their transfer record multiple times.

Ahead of the Premier League campaign, midfielder Caleb Yirenkyi joined the club for £23.1million from Nordsjaelland.

Yirenkyi's move broke the Sky Blues' record, just as Carl Rushworth's permanent switch from Brighton did beforehand.



They have also re-signed Gustavo Hamer from Sheffield United and added Loum Tchaouna and Aurele Amenda to the squad.

3 Lampard is said to have pushed for Coventry to sign Awoniyi from Forest Credit: Getty

Frank Onyeka has also joined permanently from Brentford.

Awoniyi is the next through the door, joining Haji Wright, Brandon Thomas-Asante and Ellis Simms in attack.

Wright is suffering from an injury heading into the season, having missed Coventry's entire build-up to the campaign.



So, Awoniyi may well see some game time straight after his move if Lampard wants him leading the line.

The Sky Blues take on Premier League champions Arsenal in their opening game on Friday, August 21.

talkSPORT will have live commentary of the game from Jim Proudfoot and former Crystal Palace manager Alan Pardew.

Sports.title: Marc Cucurella booed in first Real Madrid game over feud dating back two years
Sports.content:
Marc Cucurella booed in first Real Madrid game over feud dating back two years

Marc Cucurella received backlash from German supporters during his Real Madrid debut on Sunday.

The World Cup winner joined the Spanish giants from Chelsea at the start of the summer transfer window in a €60 million (£51.8m) deal.



3 After an hour, Yan Diomande and Cucurella both made their debuts, with Jude Bellingham getting his first minutes of pre-season Credit: AFP

Following the player's international triumph in America last month, the defender was handed an extended summer holiday.

His first appearance for Real Madrid came against Schalke in a pre-season clash on Sunday.

Cucurella played for a total of 30 minutes during the friendly, which ended in a 3-0 win for Los Blancos.



The 28-year-old replaced Alvaro Carreras in the 61st minute, but was greeted by a hostile reception from the crowd at the Veltins-Arena.

Why was Cucurella booed?

The Spaniard was booed by the home fans in Gelsenkirchen every time he touched the ball.



German supporters have had a distaste for the former Chelsea left-back since the Euro 2024 quarter-final between Spain and Germany.

Cucurella angered the host nation by blocking a goal bound effort from Jamal Musiala with his hand.



Referee Anthony Taylor opted against awarding a penalty, deeming the Spaniard's arm to be in a natural position close to his body.

La Roja went on to win the match and eventually win the tournament, but the decision sparked widespread outrage.

UEFA later acknowledged that a mistake had been made and that Germany should have been awarded a spot-kick.

3 Cucurella and Ibrahima Konate both joined Real Madrid from the Premier League this summer Credit: Getty



Some fans were so angry at the decision that they started a petition to get the game replayed, with more than 350,000 people signing it online.

The hostile treatment has plagued the full-back in Germany ever since, including neutral fans whistling him during the Euro 2024 semi-final against France.

Additionally, he was also booed during the Nations League final against Portugal in Munich last year.

The full-back was jeered at Bayern Munich during their Champions League clash with Chelsea last September.



The new Real Madrid recruit decided to speak positively about the milestone of making his debut for a historic club, though.

He said: "I am very happy. Behind all this, there is a lot of work, and all the effort I’ve put in over the years has been worth it.

3 Cucurella was jeered mercilessly following the Euro 2024 quarter-final Credit: Getty

"I’m very happy with everything that’s happening to me, and I hope it continues this way – winning titles. And above all, being able to enjoy this experience."



Cucurella has previously addressed the occasional booing, including after the Euro semi-final win against France.

He said: "I realised it for the first time when my name was read out before the game and a lot of people whistled.

"I thought about it a bit and then realised it was because of the handball situation.

"I didn't think much about it, but at the same time I was a bit sad that people came to the game just to boo a single player.



"Some people wasted their tickets. They could have gone to fans who would have really enjoyed the game."

Sports.title: Tottenham told they’ve spent £200million to get weaker in stunning transfer takedown
Sports.content:
Tottenham told they’ve spent £200million to get weaker in stunning transfer takedown

Tottenham have spent over £200million this summer, but they now head into the new Premier League season with a weaker squad.

That's the opinion of former Premier League striker Troy Deeney, who has launched a takedown of Spurs' big-money transfer business so far.

5 Spurs have spent over £200m this summer - but Deeney thinks they're now worse off Credit: AFP

Roberto De Zerbi has been hard at work over his first pre-season as manager after only just surviving relegation last term.

He has brought six new faces into his squad, spending a whopping £228m in total so far on just three of those players.

Sandro Tonali was signed from Newcastle for £100m, Mateus Fernandes joined from West Ham for £85m and Jan Paul van Hecke arrived in North London from Brighton for £52m.

The other arrivals - Andy Robertson, Marcos Senesi and Martin Dubravka - all joined on free transfers.

And that summer business from Tottenham has impressed talkSPORT's chief football correspondent Alex Crook.

Speaking on talkSPORT's Premier League All Access podcast, Crook said: "It looks a good window.

"They've got the experience of Andy Robertson, Marcos Senesi, Jan Paul van Hecke - albeit a big fee for a player who only had one year left on his contract.

"Then you've got Tonali for £100million, £270,000 a week... Mateus Fernandes, despite back-to-back relegations, I think is a very talented player.

"They still need a striker and a winger probably, but if they get those two signings, they're going to be up there in terms of the top five."

But Crook's positive outlook was certainly not echoed by Deeney, who quickly shared his wildly opposing view...

5 Tonali left Newcastle for Spurs in a club-record £100m deal earlier this summer Credit: Shutterstock Editorial

Are Spurs worse off after spending £200m?

Deeney launched into a takedown of the work done by De Zerbi this summer, assessing what Spurs' squad now looks like and also mentioning the sales of Cristian Romero and Djed Spence.

The ex-Watford forward appeared to be left agitated by Crook's opinion and began: "You've set me off now...

"Andy Robertson at left-back is of age now, it would be very unfair to say that he is still the player he was at Liverpool.

"He's ageing and you're losing Djed Spence, who has had a fantastic World Cup - so you've got weaker in the wide areas."

He then added: "Romero is better than the two lads they've brought in in Van Hecke and Senesi... he's leaving.

"So they're now weaker at centre-back.

5 Romero's replacements will not be as good as he was, according to Deeney Credit: Getty

5 The £85m signing of Fernandes from relegated West Ham has also been questioned Credit: Getty

"And they've brought in Dubravka to be the third choice goalie and he's probably your best choice goalkeeper... people get onto Chelsea for their goalkeepers, Spurs' goalkeepers are terrible."

The takedown then moved into midfield, with Deeney continuing: "Tonali, I rate very very highly, but also the kid Fernandes, he's not better than Kobbie Mainoo.

"He's been relegated twice and people keep telling me he's a top player... didn't he play all of those games?

"£85million is a lot of money for is apparently top player and he's going to be great. But okay, can you show me?

"And then up front, you've got Dominic Solanke, if he's fit, great... Richarlison, if he's fit, great... James Maddison, if he's fit, great... Mohammed Kudus, if he's fit, great... Dejan Kulusevski, if he's fit, great... do I need to continue?"

Deeney eventually summarised: "They've got weaker in defence from what they had originally, ageing players and lesser quality.

5 Deeney has doubts over Spurs' attacking options too heading into the season Credit: Getty

"They're getting rid of Romero, he's the best defender they've got... he was their captain and best centre-back.

"They've spent £250million-£300million and they still don't know who's going to score them ten goals this year, still don't know who's going to cross the ball into the box this year, where the assists come from."

Host Sam Matterface then asked: "[Could it be] Mathys Tel?"

To which a dismissive Deeney cheekily replied: "Pardon?"

Tottenham start their Premier League campaign on Saturday, August 22 as they take on Brentford at the Gtech Community Stadium.

Their opening game of the season will kick-off at 5:30pm.

Sports.title: Ally McCoist names three problems new Scotland boss Sebastien Pocognoli must fix now
Sports.content:
Ally McCoist names three problems new Scotland boss Sebastien Pocognoli must fix now

Ally McCoist has urged Sebastien Pocognoli to implement a new attacking approach with Scotland to take them to the next level.

Pocognoli was confirmed as Steve Clarke's successor on Sunday, signalling a new era for the Tartan Army.

6 Pocognoli is only five years into his senior coaching career Credit: Getty

Former Belgium defender Pocognoli left Monaco at the end of last season and previously led Union Saint-Gilloise in his homeland to their first league title in 90 years in 2024/25.

He replaces Clarke, who immediately stepped down after the team's disappointing World Cup group stage exit.

His side finished the group stage as the 11th best third-place team and missed out on a place in the last 32 on goal difference.

This brought an end to Clarke's seven-year stint, during which time he earned huge praise for ending Scotland's major tournament hiatus.

The 62-year-old guided them to back-to-back European Championships after a 23-year absence, while this summer's World Cup was their first appearance since 1998.

But Clarke's tenure was tinged with mixed emotions as he failed to guide the national team out of the group stage on all three occasions.

Across three major tournament appearances, Scotland managed to score just four goals, with their only win coming against Haiti at the 2026 World Cup.

Take the handbrake off

With Clarke drawing criticism for an overly cautious approach this summer, former Scotland striker McCoist admitted this has to change under new manager Pocognoli for them to finally make it out of the group stage.

He told Monday's talkSPORT Breakfast: “I think they've got to unleash them a little bit.

“First of all, Steve's done a fabulous job, right? I really do [think that]. Moaning about not getting a major tournament and all of a sudden he gets us to three, great.

6 Clarke called time on his seven-year stint as Scotland boss after their World Cup exit Credit: Getty

6 Despite huge excitement heading into the 2026 World Cup, the Tartan Army were sent packing having scored just once in three games Credit: Getty

Despite praising Clarke for his Scotland tenure, McCoist admitted his side's performances at major tournaments have been poor.

He highlighted the national team's lack of positive results at the last two European Championships and the 2026 World Cup, insisting a 0-0 draw with England at Euro 2020 and their opening game victory over Haiti this summer were their only real highlights.

McCoist continued: “We haven't performed at any of them. We had a draw at Wembley [with England].

"Poor Euro 2024, going over by Germany. The last game against Hungary was poor, we got a double deflected goal against Haiti and then a reasonable performance, I suppose, against Morocco, but disappointing.

“We never had a goal. We just looked as though we never had a goal."

Cut out defensive errors

After urging Pocognoli to introduce a more front-foot approach in his Scotland team, McCoist then insisted he must cut out costly defensive errors if they are to have a chance of getting results.

6 McCoist had a clear plan for progress for Pocognoli's Scotland Credit: talkSPORT

Grant Hanley's attempt at playing the offside trap allowed Morocco to score the only goal to beat the Tartan Army this summer, before more individual errors led to a 3-0 defeat to Brazil in their final group game.

The ex-Rangers boss added: “The first thing we've got to do is cut out stupid defensive errors, right?

"The goals that we lost at the World Cup, from our point of view, were bordering on ridiculous. They were ridiculous.

"I mean, we were up against two excellent teams in Morocco and Brazil. And the one thing you can't do is give them a goal at the start, which effectively we did, defensively."

Star players must step up

Continuing to highlight where Pocognoli must improve Scotland, McCoist called on him to get the best out of his key players.

Returning to the World Cup, he told talkSPORT Breakfast: “Our big players, I don't think, turned up for the tournament.

6 John McGinn scored Scotland's only goal at the World Cup - but McCoist believes he could have done more Credit: Getty

“I think John McGinn, who incidentally I thought had a sensational 20-25 minutes in the Super Cup and he's without doubt been tremendous for us - I don't think he had a great tournament.

“I don't think Scott McTominay had a great tournament, and we need those boys to turn up for us.

“We had such a high in the final game to qualify for it, to get us there. And then I just feel we didn't do ourselves justice at all.

“And I just feel sometimes you could maybe, and it's the easiest thing in the world to say, unleash them and go and have a go, right? I don't think we did that. I don't think we do that.

“And the proof of the pudding is you look at a team like Cape Verde, who the one thing they do, they have a goal. And they grabbed everybody's attention. I did the Argentina game, the story about the goalkeeper [Vozinha], the whole thing.

“And that would be a little bit of regret as a Scottish fan over there watching it."

6 Hampden Park will host six matches at Euro 2028, and Scotland will be desperate to qualify Credit: Getty

Despite highlighting three major areas for improvement, McCoist insisted the future is still bright for Scotland under Pocognoli.

With a joint-hosted home European Championship to come in 2028, the Rangers icon insisted the Tartan Army should feel optimistic about qualify, with two host nations getting automatic qualification.

He rounded off: “I think there's certainly talent to work with for the new manager. And I still think defensively, we're a little bit suspect.

"But the chances are hopefully good that we can get to the next Euros, obviously, with them being where they are.

“And if we do get there, I'd just like to see us have a bit more of a go, a bit more... commitment's not the right word because the commitment is obviously there, but I don’t know, unleash them a little bit.”

Sports.title: Man United stand firm on captain Bruno Fernandes' transfer stance as Galatasaray 'prepare stunning DOUBLE-your-money salary offer' and £43m bid for Portugal international
Sports.content:
Man United stand firm on captain Bruno Fernandes' transfer stance as Galatasaray 'prepare stunning DOUBLE-your-money salary offer' and £43m bid for Portugal international

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Manchester United have no plans to sell Bruno Fernandes before next month's transfer deadline.

Galatasaray, Atletico Madrid, Juventus and AC Milan are among the clubs who have been weighing up an offer for the Red Devils' captain.

It is understood Galatasaray are ready to put forward a £42.7million bid for the 31-year-old but his intention has been to stay and see if he can realise his ambition of leading United to a Premier League title challenge.

Fernandes was hurt by the club's stance last year when Al Hilal were prepared to offer £80m but he has been a model professional, leading by example and forming a close bond with coach Michael Carrick.

The Portuguese midfielder has one year left on his current deal, with an option for an additional season but is yet to agree to an extension.

A £57m release clause in his contract has now expired and United know it would take considerably more to replace him, especially in the current inflated market.

Manchester United are readying themselves for a £42.7million swoop for their captain Bruno Fernandes from Galatasaray

According to The Telegraph, Dursun Ozbek, the Galatasaray president, is on a mission to sign Fernandes and is prepared to essentially double his money.

The wage on offer is £18.3m annually, which, due to Turkey’s relaxed tax system, means he would take home twice what he earns from his near-£200,000-a-week salary at United.

The report suggests an offer from Galatasaray would feature an initial bid plus add-ons.

Performance-related add-ons reportedly include £1.3m for every title win up to £5.1m, plus £1.7m if Fernandes is the league’s top assister in his first season or £1.3m if he achieves the accolade in his second.

They could also include £850,000 if Galatasaray qualify for next season’s Champions League, plus another £850,000 if they reach the last-16 and £3m if they reach the quarter-finals.

United, meanwhile, are continuing to look for at least one more signing this summer to strengthen Carrick's hand.

However, one player who may yet leave is 22-year-old midfielder Toby Collyer, who has attracted enquiries from West Bromwich Albion.

Sports.title: Sky Sports DROP Baller League after 'partnership came to natural end' - with celebrity-backed competition 'keen to become free-to-air'
Sports.content:
Sky Sports DROP Baller League after 'partnership came to natural end' - with celebrity-backed competition 'keen to become free-to-air'

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Sports broadcasting giants Sky Sports have ended their coverage of Baller League from next season after opting not to renew their contract.

The competition, which has since its inception been backed by the likes of KSI, Gary Lineker and Ian Wright, sold out the O2 Arena for last season's final, which was won by KSI's Prime FC.

According to The Guardian, Sky are said to have been happy with viewing figures and social media interaction, but feel the partnership has come to a natural end.

The first UK edition of the tournament, which is an indoor six-a-side competition, took place in 2025 and follows a common trend of the growth in power of influencers.

The teams were usually made up of former professional footballers or those without a club, and have also been managed by the likes of Chloe Kelly and Angry Ginge.

It had first launched in Germany a year prior, inspired by Spain's Kings League, with backing from footballers Mats Hummels and Lukas Podolski.

Sky Sports had ended its partnership with Baller League, who are keen to make the competition free-to-air

Chief executive Felix Starck told The Guardian that the organisation had not tried to extend its deal with Sky and is keen to make its shows free-to-air. It is reported, though, that talks with Comcast, Sky's parent company, did take place.

They are said to now be focusing on expanding their YouTube profile.

The Baller League is made up of 12 teams and there are rolling subs throughout games.

Each team plays each other once in back-to-back matches on Monday nights, with the final four at the end of the season progressing to the semi-finals, before the final decides the winner of the league.

It's that time of the year again – the transfer window is now open until September 1 and it's sure to be a busy period as clubs look to make big signings ahead of the new season.

Here are today's latest developments from Simon Jones and the Daily Mail Sport team...

Liverpool yet to receive approach for Bajcetic

Liverpool have yet to receive an offer or enquiry from Getafe for midfielder Stefan Bajcetic.

The 21-year-old has one year left on contact and spent part of last season on loan at Las Palmas.

Madrid-based Getafe have been credited with interest but are yet to make a move.

Awoniyi completes move to newly promoted Coventry

Coventry City have completed the £9million signing of Taiwo Awoniyi from Nottingham Forest.

The Nigeria international was given a send-off at the City Ground during Forest's 2-0 pre-season win over Brest on Sunday.

Awoniyi spent four seasons at Forest, scoring 21 goals in 90 Premier League appearances.

Nottingham Forest paid tribute to Taiwo Awoniyi on Sunday ahead of his move to Coventry

Man United youngster heads for the EFL

Manchester United forward Ethan Ennis is joining Stockport County.

The 21-year-old has agreed a permanent deal for an undisclosed fee with add ons plus a 50percent sell-on and buy-back clause, while United retain matching rights too.

Ennis joined United's academy in 2021 and was in their FA Youth Cup-winning squad the following year, before being promoted to the Under-21s.

He got his first taste of senior football with a loan to Doncaster Rovers, and last season appeared 46 times as part of a temporary switch to Fleetwood Town, scoring six goals and providing eight assists.

He will link up with another former United academy product James Bailey at Edgeley Park, who secured a contract with Jimmy McNulty's side earlier this summer, following the expiry of his deal at United.

Brighton reject Rangers offer for winger

Brighton have rejected a £7.5million offer from Rangers for winger Amario Cozier-Duberry.

The winger spent last season on loan at Bolton.

Man United to rebuff Fernandes interest

Manchester United have no plans to sell Bruno Fernandes before next month's transfer deadline.

Galatasaray, Atletico Madrid, Juventus and AC Milan, are among the clubs who have been weighing up an offer for the United captain.

It's nearly Hammer time for Piroe

Leeds United have given Joel Piroe permission to travel to West Ham for a medical.

The striker is expected to travel this evening ahead of finalising his move to the Championship club.

With AZ Alkmaar digging in their heels over their valuation of Troy Parrott, the Hammers moved for Piroe on a loan deal, with an obligation to buy.

Joel Piroe is set to say goodbye to Leeds and join West Ham on loan

Ipswich land Ouattara from Strasbourg

Ipswich have confirmed the signing of versatile 20-year-old Abdoul Ouattara, reuniting him with manager Gary O'Neil.

Daily Mail Sport previously reported how the Tractor Boys have been closing in on a deal for Ouattara and team-mate Julio Enciso, 22. The pair worked with O'Neil at Strasbourg last season, before O'Neil left to replace Kieran McKenna at Portman Road.

O'Neil said: 'Abdoul is a talented young player who can play in different positions, so is a very good addition to our squad. We enjoyed working with him in France last season and are delighted to have the opportunity to do so again at Ipswich.'

Canaries making progress on Musaba talks

Norwich City are advancing in talks to sign Fenerbahce winger Anthony Musaba on a season's loan.

The 25-year-old Dutchman, formerly played for Sheffield Wednesday, is due to arrive tonight ahead of a medical.

Norwich want a winger as Ali Ahmed has injured an anterior cruciate ligament.

City work on Bouaddi deal

Manchester City and Lille working to get a deal for £85m-rated Ayyoub Bouaddi over the line.

As Daily Mail Sport reported over the weekend, Lille have been fighting to keep the midfielder for one more season, but City and the player want to seal a move now.

Lille coach Davide Ancelotti explained why Bouaddi is wanted by Manchester City following Lille’s friendly at Everton, saying: ‘Bouaddi is a very good player. He is available (in terms of his fitness) and he played 45 minutes. But that is only because I have to manage his minutes. Next week we start the season and I consider him as an available player for me.

‘Of course, there are negotiations. There is interest from so many clubs. He is a really, really good player and I hope that he is going to stay with us! What makes him so special? He has a huge personality.

‘He is incredibly intelligent on and off the pitch, he is really mature. He is 18 years old but he looks like he is 32 when he is on the pitch. Technically he is really complete. He is also physical, really strong in duels. He’s going to be one of the best midfielders in Europe for the next 10 years.’

Ayyoub Bouaddi is 'really complete' according to his Lille boss Davide Ancelotti

Chelsea set Neto price tag

Chelsea want close to £100million if they are to sell Pedro Neto this summer, sources inside the Stamford Bridge club have told Daily Mail Sport.

Neto, 26, has had several interested suitors in this window from the Premier League and beyond. Saudi side Al Hilal have been heavily linked this week.

It is understood no formal bids have yet landed with Chelsea for their Portuguese international, but they are aware of others' appreciation.

The Spain captain will then undergo a medical ahead of completing his £64.5million move to the La Liga champions.

Rodri is due to sign a four-year contract on Tuesday and the plan is for him to be unveiled by the club on Wednesday.

Former City full-back Joao Cancelo is also due in Barcelona at lunchtime today after agreeing to return to the club from Al Hilal.

Rodri is set to return to Spain after lifting the World Cup with his country this summer

Vicario lands in Turin after Spurs strike loan deal

Tottenham goalkeeper Guglielmo Vicario has arrived in Italy ahead of completing his initial loan move to Juventus.

The deal also includes an £8.5m option to buy the 28-year-old Italy international permanently.

The 29-year-old Italian has been on Juve's list for some time and they reverted to him on Sunday after a move for Aston Villa's Emiliano Martinez collapsed.

Villa are signing Zion Suzuki from Parma in a £30m deal. The Japan international is due to undergo his medical today also.

Sunderland set to confirm Methalie deal

Toulouse left-back Dayann Methalie arrived in the UK on Sunday ahead of his medical at Sunderland.

The France U21 international, a former target for Newcastle, is set to finalise his £25.7million move pending today’s tests.

Newcastle have also held talks with Bayern Munich over a move for Joao Palhinha but have other targets they are considering. Tottenham's Lucas Bergvall is one of the names that remains on their radar in the final days of the window.

Sports.title: Revealed: The mistakes Real Madrid made to cause Rodri to snub his 'dream' move to their 'ticking time bomb' and join Barcelona for £64.5m instead
Sports.content:
Revealed: The mistakes Real Madrid made to cause Rodri to snub his 'dream' move to their 'ticking time bomb' and join Barcelona for £64.5m instead

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Real Madrid’s lack of commitment and concerns over the harmony in their squad were reportedly among factors that convinced Rodri to snub his ‘dream move’ to join rivals Barcelona.

Barcelona are close to finalising a £64.5million move for Rodri after striking an agreement with Man City, with the LaLiga champions hopeful the midfielder could be unveiled at the Camp Nou on Wednesday.

Daily Mail Sport reported that Rodri is expected to sign a four-year contract.

Earlier this month, it was revealed that Rodri – who was crowned as the World Cup’s best player – had made the decision to pursue a move to Barcelona over Real Madrid.

According to Spanish newspaper Marca, Rodri had long viewed Real Madrid as his dream move and had initially wanted to join them from city rivals Atletico in 2019 before joining Man City after realising an offer was not realistic.

The report stated while Real Madrid fans had been vocal in their desire to sign Rodri this summer, the enthusiasm was not shared within the club.

Rodri is set to join Barcelona from Manchester City after snubbing a move to Real Madrid

A report has claimed a lack of enthusiasm from Real Madrid and concerns their sporting project is a 'ticking time bomb' contributed to Rodri's final decision

Back-to-back LaLiga winners Barcelona hope to seal a move for Rodri this week

Real Madrid were reported to have begun their pursuit of Rodri after the World Cup, but only president Florentino Perez and chief executive Jose Angel Sánchez called him.

Manager Jose Mourinho, by contrast, had reportedly repeatedly called Bernardo Silva and Marc Cucurella earlier in the summer while pursuing the pair.

The report claimed Real Madrid also had doubts internally over signing Rodri, with claims the midfielder ‘lingers on the ball too long’ and that the club are instead looking for a ‘more dynamic player’.

Rodri was said to have sensed Real Madrid’s lack of enthusiasm, while Barcelona boss Hansi Flick, president Joan Laporta, sporting director Deco and members of the squad had called him in a bid to convince him to move to the Nou Camp.

The report added that while both Barcelona and Real Madrid had made the same financial offer to Rodri, the former Ballon d’Or winner had preferred the stability and playing style of the former when making his decision.

While Barcelona have secured back-to-back LaLiga titles, Real Madrid endured a nightmare end to last season amid much publicised in-fighting within the camp.

Rodri is set to leave Man City following a trophy-laden spell, which has included winning four Premier League titles and the 2023 Champions League.

The Spanish star has also won two FA Cups, three Carabao Cups and helped Man City win the UEFA Super Cup and Club World Cup.

Sports.title: Actress Hayden Panettiere dead at 36: Hollywood star known for roles in Heroes and Nashville remembered for bringing 'joy to all who knew her' after shock passing
Sports.content:
See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Actress Hayden Panettiere has been remembered as 'an incredible light and a force of nature' after her death at the age of 36.

The former child star, who was known for her roles on the hit NBC series Heroes and musical drama Nashville, was found dead in Greenville, South Carolina, on Sunday afternoon. She leaves behind an 11-year-old daughter.

Representatives for Panettiere announced on Sunday: 'It is with profound sadness that we share the tragic passing of our beloved Hayden.

'She was an incredible light and a force of nature who brought immeasurable love and joy to all who knew her - and to the millions who watched her onscreen.'

Detectives confirmed to the Daily Mail that they responded to the apartment block in Greenville yesterday afternoon after they received a 911 call from an 'acquaintance' of Panettiere, describing her as 'unresponsive'.

In the dispatch audio of the call made at 1.51pm, a female dispatcher described Panettiere as suffering a 'cardiac arrest.' A few moments later a male dispatcher could be heard saying that Panettiere had suffered a suspected overdose at the home in Greenville.

Officers and paramedics carried out chest compressions while trying to save Panettiere's life at the Judson Mill Lofts apartment block.

The actress – who was due to turn 37 this Friday - was pronounced dead at the scene just over 40 minutes later at 2.32pm.

Police and the local coroner's office are probing the death, but said the 'preliminary investigation has not indicated any signs of foul play or suspicious circumstances'.

Beloved actress Hayden Panettiere has died at the age of 36. She leaves behind her daughter, who is 11. Panettiere is pictured here attending the Met Gala in 2014

Panettiere is seen on May 19, 2026 in New York City, promoting her new book. The tragic news comes just months after her memoir, This is Me, became a New York Times bestseller. The actress had become candid about her struggles dealing with fame, especially as a child star, in the months before her passing

Panettiere started out as a child star, with her first acting gig at just 11 months old

The star and her on-off real estate agent boyfriend Brian Hickerson were said to have flown from Los Angeles to South Carolina, where he is from, one day before she died.

The Hollywood star earned multiple award nominations across her career, most notably while playing cheerleader Claire Bennet on Heroes and Juliette Barnes on Nashville.

Panettiere, who was set to turn 37 on Friday, also appeared in the Scream franchise as Kirby Reed, and lent her voice to the video games Until Dawn and Kingdom Hearts.

She is predeceased by her brother, Jensen, who passed away in February 2023 from 'an enlarged heart' at the age of 28.

Panettiere recently released a memoir

Panettiere said that she felt like she 'lost half of her soul' following his death, and revealed that the stress of his loss resulted in her body 'ballooning out', which left her in a 'really bad' and 'destructive' place.

The tragic news of her death comes just months after her memoir, This is Me: A Reckoning, became a New York Times bestseller. In the book, Panettiere described how she contended with fame and handled the difficulties in her life.

She had suffered from drug addiction, beginning when she was just 15 years old. At the time, she claimed she started taking 'happy pills' in an effort to make her seem more 'peppy' during interviews.

Her addiction then became worse while she was battling postpartum depression following the birth of her daughter Kaya in 2014.

But Panettiere has been sober in recent years, she said in a 2022 interview, noting that 'it's an everyday battle.'

Hayden Panettiere is pictured playing the character Claire Bennet in the NBC sci-fi drama series Heroes

The actress's younger brother, Jansen Panettiere, passed away in February 2023 from 'an enlarged heart'. They are seen together here in 2011

Hayden Panettiere has tragically died at the age of 36. Her cause of death was not immediately clear. The Hollywood star is pictured here at a gala in Hollywood in 2022

Panettiere leaves behind an 11-year-old daughter with ex, Wladimir Klitschko

'It's an everyday choice, and I'm checking in with myself all the time,' Panettiere told People at the time. 'But I'm just so grateful to be part of this world again, and I will never take it for granted again.'

Panettiere has also told how she nearly died during childbirth, and later relinquished custody of her daughte, who now lives in Europe, to her ex, former heavyweight boxing champion Wladimir Klitschko, while struggling with postpartum depression in 2018.

Speaking of the decision, Panettiere said she 'desperately' needed help at the time and insisted that Kaya does not feel 'abandoned' while appearing in a recent episode of the On Purpose with Jay Shetty podcast.

'The idea that anybody would think that I would just give away my child and be okay with it is heartbreaking. Couldn't be further from the truth,' the actress said.

'I was struggling with mental health and anxiety and postpartum and having to act my way through it, and just feeling like I completely lost myself,' she added.

Panettiere is remembered for her role as Claire Bennet on the hit NBC series Heroes

Panettiere is seen during her book tour in New York City in May

Panettiere is seen crying following her brother's celebration of life event in their hometown of Palisades, New York

Panettiere is pictured with her daughter, after telling how she almost died during childbirth

Panettiere has also come out as bisexual while she promoted her new book, telling Us Weekly in May: 'It's sad that I had to wait till I was 36 years old to share that part of me, but better late than never, right?

'I've chosen to share it with the world, I'm comfortable saying I'm bisexual. I'm comfortable to confidently say that, yes, I am bisexual. I said it!'

Despite having little privacy due to 'paparazzi always outside waiting for me,' Panettiere still managed to secretly date women, whom she preferred to men from 'a very, very young age.'

'[I was] much more into women,' the two-time Golden Globe nominee said. 'But, yeah, I have explored it, but I don't think I ever had the courage, because I hadn't shared this with anybody.

'I didn't really have the courage to throw myself fully, emotionally into it, because then if I did fall in love, that wasn't something that I wanted to ever have to hide. I didn't feel confident enough, and I was too afraid to really let that part of me explore that part of me.'

By the age of 19, Panettiere dissolved her business relationship with her mother, who was also her manager at the time.

Panettiere came out as bisexual as she promoted her new book. The actress is pictured here as Claire Bennet in Heroes

She played Juliette Barnes on the ABC show Nashville, releasing a number of her own songs

Panettiere is pictured with actor Adrian Pasdar on the set of Heroes

Panettiere was born on August 21, 1989 in Palisades, New York, and first started acting at just 11 months old, appearing in a commercial.

Her full-time acting career then began in 1994 when she played Sarah Roberts in the ABC soap opera One Life to Live until 1997. She then went on to play Lizzie Spaulding in the CBS soap opera Guiding Light from 1996 to 2000.

For her role on Pixar's A Bug's Life, she was nominated for a Young Artist Award and Grammy Award, making her the fifth-youngest nominee for a Grammy.

Her other credits include Remember the Titans, Ally McBeal, Racing Stripes, Ice Princess and I Love You, Beth Cooper.

But it was her role as a cheerleader with superpowers in Heroes, for which she won three Teen Choice Awards, that propelled her to fame in 2006, with the series revolving around the mantra: 'Save the cheerleader, save the world.'

Panettiere has also recorded a number of songs for the films and television programs she was in, including My Hero is You for the Disney Channel film Tiger Cruise and I Fly for the Disney film Ice Princess, which she co-starred in with the late Michelle Trachtenberg.

Panettiere has opened up about her struggles with addiction, beginning when she was just 15

Her first single not associated with an acting role, the reggae-infused Wake Up Call, was digitally released on August 5, 2008.

Clothing brand Candie's announced it was premiering an ad campaign for the single in late July of that year, and provided additional promotion for the song with a television ad and a music video starring Sebastian Stan, who played Panettiere's brother in The Architect.

Panettiere later played a brash country upstart opposite Connie Britton on Nashville, which aired on ABC for four seasons before being canceled and revived on CMT.

She did her own singing for the show, earning her some hits on the country charts as well as two supporting actress Golden Globe nominations.

In total, Panettiere had 11 songs recorded for Nashville appear on Billboard´s Hot Country Songs charts during the show's run, including two featuring Britton.

Following the news of her death, actor Randall Slavin shared a photo of him with Panettiere, writing: 'Peace be with you.'

She had shared the same photo just two weeks prior, with the caption, 'Good times and good friends.'

Actress Selma Blair also wrote on Instagram: 'I love you. Don't be gone. Don't be gone. Please,' while Melissa Barrera posted to her Instagram story: 'Rest in peace sweet Hayden.'

SAG-AFTRA added that it 'mourns the sudden passing of Hayden Panettiere.'

Sports.title: Ranking of the best players in world football revealed in EA SPORTS FC27's new ratings - with just ONE Premier League player set to star in the top 10
Sports.content:
Football game company EA Sports have revealed their top-rated players for the upcoming FC27 game, with only one Premier League player making the top ten.

The newest edition of the game, formerly called FIFA, will be fully released on September 25, with fans able to play on PC, PlayStation, Xbox, Nintendo Switch, and Amazon Luna.

To build anticipation for its release, EA SPORTS have revealed official ratings, with the gradings for the world's top stars revealed.

There is no outright leader in terms of the highest rating of men's players – with Kylian Mbappe and Erling Haaland both rated 91 for the launch.

There are then a further nine players just behind them on 90 – with only one from the Premier League – but set to leave – in Rodri.

The Barcelona-bound midfielder is joined by Ousmane Dembele, Vitinha, Harry Kane, Michael Olise, Pedri, Lamine Yamal, Thibaut Courtois and Jude Bellingham.

There is set to be just one Premier League player in the top-10 highest-rated men's players in the new FC27 game

There are then three Premier League players rated 89 in Gianluigi Donnarumma, Bruno Fernandes and Gabriel.

Mbappe was also the highest-rated men's player in FC26 at 91, joined by Mohamed Salah.

There is, meanwhile, a clear front-runner in the women's selection. Alexia Putellas, who joined London City Lionesses from Barcelona this summer, takes the crown with a 91 rating, closely followed by former team-mate Aitana Bonmati and Khadija Shaw of Manchester City.

More player ratings are set to be released in the coming days, with the top Premier League stars announced at 4pm BST on Tuesday.

Sports.title: 'You've got to be nutty to try it... but it works': Why the same 'claustrophobic' tactic keeps proving England's kryptonite - and Pakistan are the perfect team to exploit it
Sports.content:
'You've got to be nutty to try it... but it works': Why the same 'claustrophobic' tactic keeps proving England's kryptonite - and Pakistan are the perfect team to exploit it

Unlock more of the best of our cricket coverage with a DailyMail+ subscription - brilliant exclusives, in-depth insight and the writers you love every day

If Pakistan have been paying attention, they will know exactly what to do when Joe Root or Harry Brook walk out to bat in Wednesday's first Test at Headingley. Babar Azam should instruct wicketkeeper Mohammad Rizwan to stand up to the stumps – and ask his seamers to swallow their pride

In an age of sometimes breathless Test cricket, the tactic has demanded pause for thought. Used to good effect by Australia’s Alex Carey during the Ashes, it was reprised by Tom Blundell during New Zealand’s 2–1 victory over England earlier this summer. Brook couldn’t get past 58, while Root averaged 28, his lowest in a series since the tour of Pakistan in late 2022.

But if his performance back then in batsman-friendly conditions felt an aberration, his drop-off against the canny New Zealanders was all part of a plan that is becoming part of Test cricket’s fabric.

In 2025, only two per cent of balls bowled by seamers in Test cricket came with the wicketkeeper standing up, with Rob Key, England’s managing director, insisting before the Ashes: ‘This 75mph, keeper up, dobbing it on a length – we know that doesn’t work in Test cricket, wherever you are.’

Then came Michael Neser and Scott Boland, backed up by the lightning-quick Carey. And if neither were as slow as 75mph, Key’s wisdom has aged like sour milk. So far in 2026, that percentage has risen above 14, as fielding captains cotton on to the benefits of keeping batsmen chained to the crease.

And against a team such as England, who under Brendon McCullum enjoyed using their feet to the quicks, it has proved a masterstroke – one that looks tailor-made for Pakistan attack leader Mohammad Abbas, who operates at a pace (around 80mph) which makes the tactic feasible, and has the control to pull it off.

England batsmen struggled when Australia wicketkeeper Alex Carey stood up to the stumps in last winter's Ashes Down Under

And it was a similar story in New Zealand's tour of England this summer, with Jordan Cox among those to fall to Matt Henry with Tom Blundell applying the pressure

Few understand its value better than the former England wicketkeeper Jack Russell, who used it to claustrophobic effect for Gloucestershire’s powerful white-ball side at the turn of the millennium.

‘It started with Craig White being a pinch hitter at Yorkshire, and we thought, "OK, we need to stop him doing that",’ he tells Daily Mail Sport in between painting canvases for a new exhibition of his artwork starting this week at London’s Chris Beetles gallery. ‘So as soon as he would open the innings, I would zoom up to the stumps.

‘There are so many benefits. Obviously keeping a batsman in his crease is the main reason. But it can affect things like lbws and nicks to the slips, because the batsman can’t get forward to cover movement so easily. We always had a first slip, and found we got a lot of wickets that way.

‘The bowlers liked it too: they could concentrate on their length, because the batters weren’t able to mess with it too much. So it made the bowlers happy, as long as their egos weren’t too big and they didn’t mind the keeper standing up. And being that close, you could get in the batsman’s minds a bit – or a lot.’

Russell is enough of a cricket historian to know that Godfrey Evans was standing up to Alec Bedser long before he stumped a startled Dean Jones down the leg side off Gladstone Small at Sydney during the 1990-91 Ashes.

But, understandably, he never dwelled too long on potential remedies for batsmen. ‘Don’t get hit on the leg,’ he says. ‘And if the pitch is reasonably flat, you can probably err on moving out to the ball and getting a straight bat on it.’

Pakistan seamer Mohammad Abbas has the control required to pull off the tactic at Headingley this week

Abbas, who operates at around 80mph, takes the wicket of West Indies' Jomel Warrican with Mohammad Rizwan stood up to the stumps earlier this year

That first piece of advice feels especially germane right now. Root has fallen lbw in six of his last nine Test innings, and Brook in three of his last seven. New Zealand’s Matt Henry, operating in the low-80mphs, was all over both at the Oval.

England, by contrast, have used the tactic only sporadically, possibly because their main bowlers – Jofra Archer, Gus Atkinson and Josh Tongue – are all a bit quicker. But wicketkeeper Jamie Smith and England fielding coach Sarah Taylor are aware of the trend.

‘It’s a really important skill,’ says Smith. ‘We have worked on it a little bit so far, but it’s trying to find the right balance. You can’t really stand up to them in the warm-ups, or I'm not sure how many hands or fingers I’d have left.’

Injury concerns aside, why don’t more teams do it? ‘Well, you've got to be brave and a bit nutty,’ says Russell, who says the pace of the bowler didn’t matter to him: at Gloucestershire, he was even known to stand up to West Indies quick Courtney Walsh. ‘You’ve got to have the keepers who are prepared to do it.’

England can’t say they haven’t been warned.

Sports.title: 'Frank Lampard has done incredible things... he's a god here': Coventry legend STEVE OGRIZOVIC on the thrill of club's top-flight return, their rollercoaster journey, the one match he'll 'never tire' of talking about and bowling Viv Richards
Sports.content:
'Frank Lampard has done incredible things... he's a god here': Coventry legend STEVE OGRIZOVIC on the thrill of club's top-flight return, their rollercoaster journey, the one match he'll 'never tire' of talking about and bowling Viv Richards

Unlock more of the best of our journalism with a DailyMail+ subscription - brilliant exclusives, in-depth insight and the writers you love every day

The very lowest ebb is difficult to locate. 'There's been a few,' admits Steve Ogrizovic, and this living legend of Coventry City exhales deeply as he begins to file through his mind in search of them.

There was administration in March 2013 and a year in exile at Northampton, but he settles on the relegation season of 2016-17, somewhere before Mark Robins returned as manager and Coventry won at Wembley. 'Going down into League Two, that was probably as low as it could get.'

Ogrizovic should know. Few have traced the fall and rise of the Sky Blues quite like the goalkeeper who made a record 601 appearances during 16 years as a player, then joined the coaching staff for 19 years and has analysed them for CWR, the BBC radio station, for the last seven years.

For 42 years, he has been at close quarters. 'The full circle,' as he tells Daily Mail Sport ahead of Coventry's return to Premier League action at Arsenal on Friday.

'I've seen the good and the bad. The road has been tough, particularly for fans and the people of the city. After being in the Premier League for so long, they didn't expect to be away for 25 years.

'So, it's nice to see the good times back again. It is really exciting and it's been exciting for the last seven years. The club has found its feet again off the pitch and that's helped managers to present a decent side on it.'

'It's nice to see the good times back again,' says Coventry legend Steve Ogrizovic. 'The club has found its feet again off the pitch'

Ogrizovic, an FA Cup winner in 1987, is Coventry's record appearance-maker, playing 601 times for the Sky Blues between 1984 and 2000

If rock bottom remains an elusive concept, the crux of the problem is easier to identify as the move from Highfield Road to the stadium now known as the CBS Arena in 2005.

'It wasn't thought out or financed properly,' says Ogrizovic. 'You could soon see there were going to be problems. There was a delay in the opening, it cost the club a lot more money than they expected and they needed a bail-out from the council. That's where it all started.'

By 2007, the financial struggles had prompted a takeover by hedge funders SISU, who ran the club badly and endured a terrible relationship with the fans. Every twist of the story forced Coventry deeper into the mire.

'Administration was a low point,' recalls Ogrizovic. 'We were cut to the bone. Cutting staff, less money spent on players, very little money spent on facilities.

'Every year there was a rallying call to say things will change and this season will be better than the last. And working at the club you wanted to believe that was going to be case, but it didn't happen and every year seemed to get worse.'

By April 2017, with Coventry plummeting into League Two, 43,000 Sky Blues fans made a trip to Wembley as their beleaguered team beat Oxford and won the Checkatrade Trophy, less than a month after Robins returned for his second spell in charge.

'It surprised a lot of people outside Coventry,' says Ogrizovic. 'It showed the fanbase was still there and people still cared about the club and wanted to get behind them. We'd been in decline to the point of relegation to League Two and that was a significant turning point.'

Ogrizovic and Coventry enjoyed some good times at Highfield Road, but the club's decline started when they moved to what is now the CBS Arena in 2005

'Football is only exciting and enjoyable because of what the fans bring to the occasion,' says Ogrizovic, who is full of praise for the Coventry fans who have been through the mill

Ogrizovic joined Coventry in 1984, a point halfway through the club's 34 years in the top flight, and was surely the best £72,500 they ever spent.

He came from Shrewsbury, who were then in the second tier, having spent five years as understudy to Ray Clemence at Liverpool learning his trade from the best team in the world and acquiring good habits, not to mention a couple of medals as a non-playing substitute in the European Cup finals of 1978 and 1981.

His two years with the Shrews enabled him to enjoy another passion, playing cricket for Shropshire and the Minor Counties. Ogrizovic was a medium-quick right-armer who talks just as affectionately of his cricketing achievements as his footballing ones.

Among them, beating Geoff Boycott's Yorkshire in the NatWest Trophy of 1984 and playing against a Somerset team featuring Viv Richards, Ian Botham and Joel Garner, in the previous year.

'I've got a picture at home of the great man's leg peg cartwheeling out of the ground,' says Ogrizovic. 'People see it and say, "Is that Viv Richards?", and I say, "Yes". What I don't tell them is it was a no ball!'

From his debut, Ogrizovic played a then-record 246 consecutive games for Coventry until an injury in September 1989. Together with two ever-present seasons for Shrewsbury, he did not miss a game for more than seven years.

And there is one game during those seven years which attracts more attention than the others. 'Not a day goes by without someone coming up to talk to me about the FA Cup final in 1987 (a 3-2 win over Tottenham),' says Ogrizovic.

'People tell me where they were and what they were doing. I know there were 100,000 in the stadium but I'm sure I've spoken to more than 100,000 people who were there and that's great. I'll never tire of it.

Ogrizovic and his Coventry team-mates celebrate winning the 1987 FA Cup, beating Spurs 3-2 in a classic

Receiving the PFA Merit Award alongside Michael Owen (Young Player of the Year) and Dennis Bergkamp (Player of the Year) in 1998

'Football is only exciting and enjoyable because of what the fans bring to the occasion. They were incredible on that FA Cup run. It's all about the journey, how we got there, what we went through, an exciting final... but if anyone asks for a defining moment it's the relief at the final whistle when you've achieved a boyhood dream of winning the FA Cup.'

Similar emotions were involved when Coventry escaped relegation, proving those wrong who wrote them off. In 1985, winning the last three games. In 1997, with a last-day win at Tottenham.

There were plenty of other examples across 34 years in the top flight. They finally succumbed to the drop in 2001, a year after Ogrizovic had retired from playing at the age of 42 and joined the coaching staff.

'It can feel almost as good as winning something,' he says. 'We weren't always at the bottom but never had a lot of money compared to others so had to be clever in the transfer market, get recruitment right and develop players.

'Coventry is a proud club with a brilliant fanbase and relied on team spirit and cohesion to punch above their weight. I see the same traits now. Connections between the players and fans. Connections among the players. You see it and feel it, but nobody can measure it.

'Sports scientists can't measure it. They can measure lots of things with data but not the strength of team spirit and what those bonds give you. You can't convert that into points, but you know and feel when it's there and anybody who plays sport will understand the value of that.'

Ogrizovic, who will be at the Emirates on Friday on broadcasting duty, has savoured the climb back from League Two. Promotion via the play-offs in 2018 and up as League One champions in 2020, then the near miss at Wembley, beaten on penalties by Luton in 2023, a year before they lost on penalties to Manchester United in an FA Cup semi-final.

Along the way came Doug King's takeover from SISU and his decision to sack Robins and install Lampard. 'Mark Robins did a brilliant job,' says Ogrizovic. 'He had taken us from League Two to the brink of the Premier League and a toenail from an FA Cup final and when he was sacked it wasn't a popular decision, and it can't have been easy to take over.

'Frank Lampard has done incredible things,' says Ogrizovic of the man who will lead Coventry out when they make their top-flight return at the Emirates on Friday

'Frank Lampard has done incredible things. He's carried the baton, made some slight changes but has been committed to attacking football – as we were under Robins. We've gained momentum and become more consistent and it's got us to the Premier League. He's a god in Coventry at the moment.'

King's status is not far behind. 'A breath of fresh air,' says Ogrizovic. 'One of the greatest things was to give Coventry City ownership of its stadium again.'

That move came last year and was followed by Lampard's team winning the Championship title.

'Coventry's story is unique,' says Ogrizovic. 'It's a good one but there are clubs with similar stories, look at Leicester 10 years after winning the Premier League are in League One. They'll be back.

'Football has a habit of turning full circle. This is what football does, this is why it's so exciting, this is why we love it because if you've been through the pain of the bad times, you will enjoy the good times.'

Sports.title: 'Brutal, searing and punishing heat' - Babb on playing for Ireland at USA '94
Sports.content:
While none of the home nations qualified for the 1994 World Cup, the Republic of Ireland did.

It was a second successive appearance at the tournament for the Boys in Green, who were again led by 1966 World Cup winner Jack Charlton.

At Italia '90, the weather had been hot - but at USA '94, it was a different kettle of fish altogether.

The iconic image of Charlton launching an open bottle of water in the direction of Andy Townsend and Tommy Coyne always provides a reminder of that.

Image: Jack Charlton led the Republic of Ireland at Italia '90 and USA '94

He clashed with FIFA over their policy that bottles could not be thrown to the players on the pitch, so took to throwing the contents instead before FIFA later relented and allowed water bags to be thrown.

"They trust me to do what is right for them and I will continue to do it," Charlton said. "We have been right in pursuing this matter and FIFA's change of heart proves that."

Charlton was rarely seen without his white baseball cap that summer. Steve Staunton famously even wore one during the national anthem before the second group game against Mexico.

One of the players in the Ireland squad that summer was Phil Babb. The defender, then 23, had just completed his second full Premier League season at Coventry.

He made his international debut in a 0-0 friendly draw with Russia in March 1994, then played in the next four friendlies leading up to the tournament.

Image: Phil Babb played in all four of the Republic of Ireland's games at the 1994 World Cup

Nothing was set in stone, but he knew he would at least have a decent chance of being included in Charlton's 22-man squad, so started to physically prepare himself.

"A coach at Coventry asked me if I wanted to do anything specific - we ended up doing 12-minute sessions in a sauna!" Babb recalls, with a smile.

"We were doing burpees, press-ups, just trying to acclimatise to that intense heat. We did about six sessions - but I wouldn't recommend it for anyone now!

"I was a fit lad and had played pretty much all the Premier League games Coventry had played that season. I adapted to the heat pretty well, but I know some of the older lads really struggled."

Babb started alongside Paul McGrath in the heart of defence for Ireland's tournament opener at Giants Stadium in New Jersey.

Image: Ray Houghton's stunning strike earned a shock 1-0 win over Italy

That Saturday, they shocked an Italy side that featured Paolo Maldini, Franco Baresi and Roberto Baggio. John Aldridge's stunner sealed a memorable 1-0 win.

It was an achievement made all the more impressive by the fact the Azzurri went on to finish as runners-up - but also given the fact it was played in temperatures exceeding 30C.

"When we walked out onto the field, about two hours before kick-off, you could tell it was going to be absolutely roasting," he recalls.

"You could tell that straight away and we didn't stay out long. I just checked the grass to see which studs I wanted, then I went straight back in. I know some of the lads were walking around and taking the atmosphere in, but I thought: 'This is too hot'.

"I didn't go out for a warm-up with the rest of the lads, either. I stayed in the changing room. It was built for NFL, so they had a 40m sprint track. I warmed up in there and waited until we went out. It was brutal, it was searing, it was punishing.

"It affected everyone's game. You were saturated after just 10 minutes walking onto a pitch, so you had to conserve energy at the right times.

"Recovery was very basic and there was very little ball work because of the demands of the actual games and the fluids you lose. When you're that dehydrated, it's quite difficult. You want a drink, but you don't feel hungry and that is a key part of the recuperation."

Image: Babb, whose Ireland were knocked out by Dennis Bergkamp's Netherlands, joined Liverpool later that summer

Thirty-two years on from that tournament, football has evolved exponentially.

Sports science has taken on a key role in the game and, this summer, is likely to play into the way teams approach games tactically due to the heat. A slower tempo is expected in many.

Charlton was not prepared to facilitate the same in 1994, though.

"We only played one way, so if you tried to go off-piste, Jack would certainly let you know!" adds Babb.

"We had one style of play, with a lone striker. If it wasn't Tommy Coyne, it might have been Niall Quinn up there and we'd be putting long balls up to him, with either willing runners out wide or the midfield bombing on.

"That was the Irish way back then. Tommy ran tirelessly, to the point where he actually collapsed with heat exhaustion on the plane home.

"I think Jack's sports science was a barrel of Guinness in his room and he'd call the lads in and have a pint! I'm sure there's a high calorific content in that, so maybe he was ahead of his time!"

YouTube YouTube , which may be using cookies and other technologies. To show you this content, we need your permission to use cookies.
